problems.title: A wet crystal
problems.problem:
Problem 1. A wet crystal

The hydrate of a stable salt $\mathbf{X}$ contains 2.79% H, 9.97% C, and 38.48% of element $\mathbf{A}$. When $\mathbf{X}$ is heated at $800\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, an oxide $\mathbf{Y}$ ($w_\mathrm{O} = 14.73\%$) is formed. When $\mathbf{X}$ is heated at a lower temperature, compound $\mathbf{Z}$ containing 5.80% C, 27.07% O, and 67.13% of element $\mathbf{A}$ is formed.

a) Write the chemical formulas of compounds $\mathbf{X}$–$\mathbf{Z}$.

b) Write equations of the described reactions.

problems.title: So similar but not the same
problems.problem:
Problem 2. So similar but not the same

A solution contains sulfates of four metals. The metals are located in the same period (of the periodic table), next to each other, and in sulfates, their oxidation number is equal to +2. The quantities of the salts are 0.0100, 0.0100, 0.0200, and 0.0200 mole. $\ce{NH3.H2O}$ and $\ce{H2O2}$ were added to the solution in excess. The resulting precipitate $\mathbf{A}$ was filtered and calcined to a constant mass of 2.47 g. After the filtrate was boiled, 2.36 g of precipitate $\mathbf{B}$ was obtained. The remaining solution contained no metal ions. Precipitate $\mathbf{A}$ was dissolved in an $\ce{HCl}$ solution, releasing $224\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of chlorine (STP). When precipitate $\mathbf{B}$ was dissolved in an $\ce{HCl}$ solution, $150\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of chlorine (STP) was released.

a) Write the chemical formulas of metal sulfates.

b) Calculate the mole amounts of these sulfates.

c) Write equations of the described reactions.

problems.title: Do not drink it
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Do not drink it

5.000 g of the characteristic odorless liquid $\mathbf{A}$ was burned in oxygen. The resulting products were absorbed in excess $\ce{NaOH}$. The mass of the alkali solution increased by 16.41 g. $\ce{Ba(OH)2}$ was added to the solution, resulting in 59.74 g of precipitate. The precipitate was dissolved by heating in hydrochloric acid, and $6.660\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of gas (STP) was released.

a) Write the empirical formula of compound $\mathbf{A}$.

b) Write all the possible structures of substance $\mathbf{A}$.

problems.title: Organic siblings
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Organic siblings

Write the structures of all such neutral, stable organic compounds whose molecules consist of C, H, and O (with empirical formulas $\mathrm{C}_m\mathrm{H}_n$ and $\mathrm{C}_m\mathrm{H}_n\mathrm{O}_x$) in which the number of carbon atoms is between 2 and 6, and all are in $sp^2$ hybridization and structurally equivalent to each other.

problems.title: Organic riddle
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Organic riddle

Substance $\mathbf{A}$ consists of 69.77% carbon and 11.63% hydrogen. Two peaks are recorded in the mass spectrum of substance $\mathbf{A}$: $m/z = 86$ (molecular ion) and $m/z = 57$. In the infrared spectrum, the line is around $1740\text{-}1720\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$. In $^{1}\mathrm{H}$ NMR spectrum, two singlet $\delta_1 = 1\text{–}1.5\ \mathrm{ppm}$ and $\delta_2 = 9.5\text{–}10\ \mathrm{ppm}$. The ratio of peak intensities is 9 : 1.

a) Write the structural formula of substance $\mathbf{A}$.

b) Write reaction equations in which substance $\mathbf{A}$ reacts with i) formaldehyde, ii) acetaldehyde in an alkaline medium, and iii) aluminum isopropanolate in the presence of isopropanol.

problems.title: Hemerythrin
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Hemerythrin

The protein hemoglobin is widely known as an oxygen transporter. Less well-known are other natural proteins capable of transporting oxygen. One of these, hemerythrin, has been found in some vertebrates. The oxygen-binding center of hemerythrin contains two iron atoms that form a complex by interacting with the side chains of amino acid residues. X-ray structural analysis showed that the distance between iron atoms in hemerythrin is 3.57 Å (in the crystal of metallic iron, the interatomic distance is 2.48 Å). One of the atoms is linked by coordination bonds with three, the other with two amino acid side chains (each chain contains a five-membered cycle). In addition, the iron atoms are linked to two other different amino acid residues by FeO coordination bonds.

a) What amino acid residues are included in the complex?

b) Draw the spatial structure of the oxygen-binding center.

c) How and where can oxygen be bound in this center?

d) What features of oxygen binding by hemoglobin do you know?

problems.title: Toxic gold
problems.problem:
Problem 7. Toxic gold

During the electrolysis of a gold cyano complex in an alkaline solution, 0.460 g of gold is precipitated at the cathode, and $13.06\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of oxygen (STP) is released at the anode. Write the electrode reactions and determine the degree of oxidation of gold in the complex, assuming that all reactions occur in 100% yield.

problems.title: Basic acid reactions
problems.problem:
Problem 8. Basic acid reactions

$1\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of solution contained 0.365 g $\ce{HCl}$ and 6.00 g $\ce{CH3COOH}$ ($K_\mathrm{a} = 1.75\cdot10^{-5}$). 2.00 g of solid sodium hydroxide was added to the solution. Calculate the pH of the solution before and after adding $\ce{NaOH}$.

problems.title: Famous for not just the wine
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Famous for not just the wine

The Burgundy mixture is prepared from $\ce{CuSO4.5H2O}$ and $\ce{Na2CO3}$ (soda) and is used to protect plants from fungal diseases. In agriculture, 1% of $\ce{CuSO4.5H2O}$ (by mass) is prepared and dissolved in an equivalent soda solution to produce 1% Burgundy mixture. To prepare the Burgundy mixture, a gardener took soda with 50% excess. Then, he added $\ce{CuSO4}$ solution to the soda solution. The mixing was carried out in a zinc-coated vessel. Due to carelessness, instead of soda ash ($\ce{Na2CO3}$), the gardener took crystalline soda ($\ce{Na2CO3.10H2O}$), assuming it is an anhydrous salt.

a) Write equations of the described reactions.

b) Estimate the mass percentage of soluble substances in the resulting solution.

problems.title: Unstable chemical
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Unstable chemical

Substance $\mathbf{A}$ decomposes spontaneously. The half-life of substance $\mathbf{A}$ at $30\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is 318 seconds, and at $24.7\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ – 460 seconds. How much time is needed for substance $\mathbf{A}$ to decay 99% at $35\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

problems.title: All the kinds of soda
problems.problem:
Problem 3. All the kinds of soda

The enthalpies of dissolution of $\ce{Na2CO3}$, $\ce{Na2CO3.H2O}$ and $\ce{Na2CO3.10H2O}$ are $-24.6\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, $-10.5\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, and $66.6\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively.

a) Calculate the enthalpies of hydration of the following reactions.

$$\begin{array}{ll} (1) & \ce{Na2CO3 + H2O -> Na2CO3.H2O} \\ (2) & \ce{Na2CO3 + 10H2O -> Na2CO3.10H2O} \\ (3) & \ce{Na2CO3.H2O + 9H2O -> Na2CO3.10H2O} \end{array}$$

10.0 grams of $\ce{Na2CO3.10H2O}$ was dissolved in 10.0 grams of water.

b) Calculate the molar fraction of $\ce{Na2CO3}$ in the solution.

c) Calculate the pH of the solution ($K_\mathrm{a1} = 4.45\cdot10^{-7}$, $K_\mathrm{a2} = 4.69\cdot10^{-11}$; $\rho = 1.2\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$).

problems.title: Copper nitrate
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Copper nitrate

19.1 grams of copper was dissolved in $189\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 40.0% nitric acid ($\rho = 1.25\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$) which gave off $6.72\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of gases (STP) with a density of 1.93 relative to air.

a) Which gases were released and in what ratio?

b) Write equations of the described reactions.

c) How much unreacted nitric acid remained in the solution?

problems.title: A simple lead battery
problems.problem:
Problem 5. A simple lead battery

Hydrogen and $\ce{Pb}$/$\ce{Pb(OH)2}$ electrodes were used to make a galvanic cell with $\ce{KOH}$ electrolyte.

a) Write the reactions occurring at the electrodes (the hydrogen electrode, in this element, is the negative electrode).

b) Write an equation to calculate the EMF and show that the EMF does not depend on the concentration of the solution.

c) Calculate the solubility product value of $\ce{Pb(OH)2}$ at $25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, knowing that EMF = 0.261 V, the standard potential of lead with respect to $[\ce{Pb^{2+}}]$ is $E^\circ(\ce{Pb^{2+}}/\ce{Pb}) = -0.126\ \mathrm{V}$, and $K_\mathrm{w} = 10^{-14}$.

problems.title: Three children of cyclohexane
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Three children of cyclohexane

Three cyclohexane derivatives, $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$, contain the same percentage of chlorine – 73.20%. In a $4.70\cdot10^{-3}$ molar sodium hydroxide solution in ethanol, the reaction rates of $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$ were measured at the same concentration ($8\cdot10^{-4}$ M). Substance $\mathbf{B}$ did not react. The reaction rate constants for compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ were 0.167 and $0.0435\ \mathrm{dm^3\,mol^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$, respectively. In both reactions, only one product (a diene) was formed.

a) Explain why the reaction rate constants are different.

b) Draw structural formulas of $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{C}$. Label the absolute configurations for $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{C}$.

c) Write the reaction equations.

problems.title: The smell of Baltics
problems.problem:
Problem 7. The smell of Baltics

Terpenoids consist of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene) fragments and contain different functional groups (hydroxyl, etc.). These compounds have a pleasant odor and are found in the essential oils of plants. Terpene $\mathbf{A}$ is a cyclohexane derivative, which is oxidized to ketone $\mathbf{B}$ with chromic acid. Dehydration of $\mathbf{A}$ produces compound $\mathbf{C}$, which contains 86.96% carbon and 13.04% hydrogen. When $\mathbf{C}$ is hydrogenated, compound $\mathbf{D}$ is formed. Ozonolysis of product $\mathbf{C}$ with water yields substance $\mathbf{E}$. Oxidation of substance $\mathbf{E}$ under severe conditions yields a mixture of various acids and $\ce{CO2}$. It is possible to isolate 3-methylpropane-1,3-dicarboxylic acid ($\beta$-methyl- glutaric acid) from the mixture.

a) Draw the structures of $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{E}$.

b) Write all the described reaction equations.

c) Which plant essential oils contain substances $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{C}$.

problems.title: Another fossil fuel
problems.problem:
Problem 8. Another fossil fuel

0.10 grams of a hydrocarbon was burned, and the gaseous products were passed through $30\underline{0}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.0200 molar $\ce{Ba(OH)2}$ solution, resulting in 0.850 g of precipitate. The $^{1}$H NMR spectrum of this carbohydrate consists of one quartet. X-ray structural analysis showed that the lengths of C–C bonds between all carbon atoms in the hydrocarbon are the same. Write the structural formulas of three hydrocarbons that meet the conditions.

problems.title: Shapeshifting organics
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Shapeshifting organics

Compound $\mathbf{X}$ turns into hydrocarbon $\mathbf{Y}$ via reduction and rearrangement in the presence of $\ce{HBF4}$. The reverse intermolecular rearrangement occurs by heating the potassium salt of the oxidation product of the compound $\mathbf{Y}$ in $\ce{CO2}$ atmosphere. After treatment with $\ce{D2O}$, the NMR spectrum of compound $\mathbf{X}$ presents a singlet at $\delta = 8.1$ (DMSO). 1.4 times less oxygen is needed for the complete burning of 1 mole of compound $\mathbf{X}$ compared to the same amount of $\mathbf{Y}$.

a) Write the chemical equations for all the reactions.

b) Write the mechanisms of the rearrangements.

problems.title: Oxidation of rhenium
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Oxidation of rhenium

Compound $\mathbf{X}$ [$w(\mathrm{Re}) = 68.16\%$] turns into compound $\mathbf{Y}$ according to the following scheme:

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|} \hline c_\mathrm{X}\ [\mathrm{M}] & A(346\ \mathrm{nm}) & A(330\ \mathrm{nm}) \\ \hline 8.4422 & 0.1815 & 0.291 \\ \hline 8.5924 & 0.1847 & 0.295 \\ \hline 8.7989 & 0.1883 & 0.302 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-1995-2-fig1.png

The results of absorption spectroscopic measurements of standard solutions of $\mathbf{X}$ are in the Table. Two more measurements were made as follows. 1.0360 g of compound $\mathbf{Y}$ was treated with hydrogen peroxide. The excess of the reagent was removed by boiling.

i) The solution was quantitatively transferred into a $500.34\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ volumetric flask, $2.50\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of concentrated $\ce{H2SO4}$ was added, and the flask was filled to the line. Result: at $A(346\ \mathrm{nm}) = 0.1844$.

ii) $50.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the solution a was pipetted into a $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ volumetric flask, $0.250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of concentrated $\ce{H2SO4}$ was added, and the flask filled to the line. Result: at $A(330\ \mathrm{nm}) = 0.294$.

Write the chemical formulas of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$. Show your calculations.

problems.title: Silver energy
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Silver energy

The EMF of a silver-zinc cell $\ce{Zn}\,|\,\ce{ZnSO4}(\mathrm{l})\,||\,\ce{AgNO3}(\mathrm{l})\,|\,\ce{Ag}$ is 1.562 V if the concentrations of the solutions are 1 M at $T = 25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

a) Write the equations of the reactions in the whole cell and at single electrodes if current is taken from the cell.

b) Calculate the EMF of the cell after 20 days of running at 0.050 A.

problems.title: The kinetics of March test
problems.problem:
Problem 4. The kinetics of March test

The kinetics of the decomposition of $\ce{AsH3}$ was studied by measuring pressure in a closed glass tube. The initial pressure of gaseous $\ce{AsH3}$ in the tube was 86.1 kPa. After 2 hours, the pressure in the tube was 112.6 kPa. The formed $\ce{As}$ condensed on the walls of the glass tube.

a) Write the chemical equation of the decomposition reaction.

b) Calculate the pressure in the glass tube after the reaction is completed.

c) Calculate the rate constant and the rate of the reaction.

d) Calculate the time necessary to decompose 99.9% of $\ce{AsH3}$.

problems.title: A lot of heating
problems.problem:
Problem 5. A lot of heating

5.5541 g of a crystalline hydrate was heated at $100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Its mass decreased to 4.1128 grams. The remnant was heated at $150\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to obtain 2.0818 g of a gas with a volume of $7.044\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ at $150\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $10\underline{0}000\ \mathrm{Pa}$. The remnant of the other heating (2.0310 g) was treated with overheated steam to obtain 1.5910 g of a solid oxide containing 20.11% oxygen. All the mentioned heatings were carried out to constant weight.

a) Write the chemical formula of the crystalline hydrate. Show your calculations.

b) Write the chemical equations of all the reactions.

problems.title: Don’t starve
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Don’t starve

The oxidation of glucose is the human organism's primary energy source. However, while starving, the reserve of hydrocarbons is diminishing, and the oxidation of two monocarbonic acids, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$, becomes the main energy source. The acids $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ turn easily into one another due to an enzymatic redox reaction. Acid $\mathbf{A}$ contains 47.06% C and 5.88% H; $\mathbf{B}$ contains 46.15% C and 7.70% H. Acid $\mathbf{A}$ decomposes slowly and spontaneously in blood, giving a volatile compound $\mathbf{C}$ that can be smelled in the air exhaled by a starving person. The density of the vapors of the compound $\mathbf{C}$ is 2.00 with respect to the air, and there is only one peak in its $^{1}$H NMR spectrum. Write the structural formulas of $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$.

problems.title: Organic riddle
problems.problem:
Problem 7. Organic riddle

Compound $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C16H15NO2}$) dissolves only in concentrated sulfuric acid and reacts with hydrazine to form a precipitate. Compound $\mathbf{A}$ was hydrolyzed in an alkaline solution. Compound $\mathbf{B}$ was separated from the solution by extracting it with ether. The remnant was acidified to separate a solid compound $\mathbf{C}$ with a molar mass of $164\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$. Compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ react with an alkaline solution of iodine to give a precipitate $\mathbf{D}$. The other product that formed in the reaction from compound $\mathbf{C}$ was turned into acid $\mathbf{E}$ by the agency of an acid. One mole of $\ce{NaOH}$ reacts with 83 g of the acid $\mathbf{E}$. Heating the acid $\mathbf{E}$ results in compound $\mathbf{F}$, which does not react with sodium hydrogen carbonate. Boiling compound $\mathbf{F}$ in water for a long time returns it to compound $\mathbf{E}$.

Compound $\mathbf{B}$ has an unpleasant smell, and it dissolves in a 5% solution of $\ce{HCl}$. It reacts with an acidified solution of sodium nitrite to liberate a gas and form compound $\mathbf{G}$, which is insoluble in water but reacts with sodium. Compound $\mathbf{G}$ is oxidized with chromosulfuric acid to give compound $\mathbf{H}$. Melting $\mathbf{H}$ with $\ce{NaOH}$ gives benzene.

a) Write the structural formulas of compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{H}$.

problems.title: Removal of iron from water
problems.problem:
Problem 8. Removal of iron from water

At what pH of the solution does $\ce{FeS}$ begin to precipitate if the initial concentration of the cation is 0.01 M, the total concentration of all the forms of sulfide ions in the solution is also 0.01 M, the dissociation constants for dihydrogen sulfide are $K_1 = 1\cdot10^{-7}$ and $K_2 = 1\cdot10^{-13}$ and the solubility product for $\ce{FeS}$ is $K_\mathrm{sp} = 1\cdot10^{-18}$? At what pH of the solution could the precipitation of $\ce{FeS}$ be considered complete (i.e. 99.9% of the initial amount of the cation has precipitated)?

problems.title: An unknown alloy
problems.problem:
Problem 1. An unknown alloy

1.0000 g of powder of a mixture of two metals was heated at $300\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in a stream of $\ce{NO2}$. As a result, 0.6683 g of light yellow substance $\mathbf{A}$ ($w_\mathrm{O} = 25.18\%$) was distilled off, and 0.7149 g of red powder remained in the reaction vessel. The reaction of $\mathbf{A}$ with concentrated hydrochloric acid produced $129.9\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of gas and $25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and 100.2 kPa. The density of this gas under these conditions is $2.8689\ \mathrm{g\,dm^{-3}}$. After the excess hydrochloric acid was neutralized with $\ce{KOH}$, a compound with a chlorine content of 44.21% was isolated. This compound was dissolved in hydrochloric acid, and upon the addition of zinc, one of the parent metals was obtained.

a) Identify two metals in the original mixture.

b) Write equations for all reactions.

problems.title: Old-school hydrogen
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Old-school hydrogen

One industrial method of hydrogen production is the Mark-1 thermodynamic cycle:

$$\begin{array}{llll} \text{i)} & \ce{CaBr2 + 2H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + 2HBr} & \text{iii)} & \ce{HgBr2 + Ca(OH)2 -> CaBr2 + HgO + H2O} \\ \text{ii)} & \ce{2HBr + Hg -> HgBr2 + H2} & \text{iv)} & \ce{2HgO -> 2Hg + O2} \end{array}$$

A second purely thermodynamic hydrogen production cycle, Mark-8, was developed by the author of Mark-1 two years later. The Mark-8 cycle, like the Mark-1 cycle, utilizes water and thermal energy. The Mark-8 cycle involves the manganese compounds $\ce{MnCl2}$, $\ce{Mn3O4}$, and $\ce{MnO2}$, as well as $\ce{HCl}$, $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{H2}$, and $\ce{O2}$. Oxygen is released at 1170 K from manganese dioxide; the other two reactions occur at 970 K and 370 K.

a) Write the reaction equations occurring in the Mark-8 cycle.

b) Explain the advantages of each of the cycles.

problems.title: On cobalt and ammonia
problems.problem:
Problem 3. On cobalt and ammonia

For the determination of the ligand molecule number in complex cation $\ce{Co(NH3)}_n^{2+}$, the EMF of the following electrochemical cell $\ce{Co}\,|\,0.05\ \mathrm{M}\ \ce{CoCl2} + x\ \mathrm{M}\ \ce{NH3 * H2O}\,|\,1.00\ \mathrm{M}\ \ce{NaOH}\,|\,\ce{HgO}\,|\,\ce{Hg}$ at $25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ was determined at various concentration of dissolved ammonia. The gas phase was, in all cases, in equilibrium with the solution. Calculate the $n$ value using data given in the table assuming that in all solutions $[\ce{Co^{2+}}] \ll [\ce{Co(NH3)}_n^{2+}]$, thus $[\ce{Co(NH3)}_n^{2+}] \approx \mathrm{const.}$

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{EMF [V]} & 0.619 & 0.659 & 0.683 & 0.715 \\ \hline p(\ce{NH3})\ \text{mmHg} & 27.8 & 44.7 & 63.4 & 107.7 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

problems.title: Combustion of acid vapors
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Combustion of acid vapors

At 1000 K and pressure $10^{5}$ Pa, the degrees of dissociation of water vapor and hydrogen chloride are $2.48\cdot10^{-7}$ and $1.10\cdot10^{-3}$, correspondingly. Calculate the value of equilibrium constant and Gibbs free energy change for the reaction $\ce{4HCl + O2 <=> 2Cl2 + 2H2O}$.

problems.title: Determining molecular mass without a mass spectrometer
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Determining molecular mass without a mass spectrometer

Organic compound $\mathbf{A}$ (melting point $167\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$) consists of two elements. The mass fraction of element $\mathbf{X}$ is 88.8%. In the $^{1}$H-NMR spectrum of compound $\mathbf{A}$, there is only one signal (singlet, $\delta = 2.34$ m.d.). To determine the molecular weight by cryoscopy, 0.040 g of compound $\mathbf{A}$ was fused with 0.50 g of camphor – the melting point of the mixture was $159\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (melting point of pure camphor is $178\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, cryoscopic constant $K = 39.7\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$). Heating substance $\mathbf{A}$ in potassium permanganate solution, substance $\mathbf{B}$ ($w_\mathbf{X} = 42.1\%$). Heating $\mathbf{B}$ in excess of acetic anhydride yielded substance $\mathbf{C}$, which also consists of two elements and the mass fraction of element $\mathbf{X}$ in the substance is 50.0%.

a) Write the chemical formulas of $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{C}$.

b) Write the equations for all reactions.

problems.title: Chemical hormones
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Chemical hormones

The widespread use of insecticides causes a disturbance of the ecological balance, which makes it relevant to use pheromones to monitor this insect and to keep it under control. The main active substance of pheromone is 1,7-dioxaspiro(5,5)undecane – compound $\mathbf{X}$. It is synthesized from δ-valerolactone.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-1996-6-fig1.png

a) Identify the intermediate compound $\mathbf{A}$.

b) Compound $\mathbf{X}$ exists in a single configuration. Draw the structure of this configuration and note the stereoelectronic effects that make it stable.

c) Identify peaks in the $^{1}$H NMR spectrum of compound $\mathbf{X}$ at 3.52 (2H) and 3.65 (2H).

Feramon also contains compound $\mathbf{Y}$. The scheme of its production is as follows:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-1996-6-fig2.png

d) The halogenation of a carbonyl compound occurs via an enolic intermediate $\mathbf{X}$ (acetal). Write the mechanism of bromination of $\mathbf{X}$.

Upon treatment of brominated $\mathbf{X}$ with potassium tert-butoxide in dimethyl sulfoxide at $110\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, compound $\mathbf{B'}$ reacted completely. On further heating for 6 hours, compound $\mathbf{B}$ reacts completely as well. In both cases, compound $\mathbf{C}$ is formed.

e) Write the structural formulas of $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{B'}$. Explain the reactivity of compounds $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{B'}$ in terms of the reaction mechanism.

Compound $\mathbf{C}$ is converted into diastereoisomers $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Y'}$ ($M = 172\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) by stereospecific hydration in THF (tetrahydrofuran). The ratio of the stereoisomers $\mathbf{Y} : \mathbf{Y'} = 18 : 1$.

f) Write their structural formulas and write reaction equations for each stage. Identify the structural effects that cause the preferential formation of compound $\mathbf{Y}$.

g) Write the absolute configurations of all chiral atoms in compounds $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Y'}$.

problems.title: Simple electrolysis
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Simple electrolysis

The $\ce{CuSO4}$ solution was subjected to electrolysis for 30.0 hours with very intense stirring. During electrolysis, the current density was 1.00 A, and all the copper (31.75 g) from the solution precipitated.

a) Which newly formed compound remains in solution?

b) What amount (in moles) of this substance was formed?

c) What volume of gas (under normal conditions) is released at the anode and cathode?

d) Write reaction equations for all the processes.

problems.title: Mercury from a gemstone
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Mercury from a gemstone

One of the methods for obtaining mercury is the calcination of mercury(II) sulfide cinnabar with calcium oxide at $600$–$700\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. 500.00 g of cinnabar containing iron(II) sulfide was heated with 170.00 g of calcium oxide. 393.16 g of mercury was distilled off, the reducing agent was oxidized to the maximum. The gray residue was extracted in a Soxhlet extractor for a long time. From the original gray residue, 43.98 g of black powder $\mathbf{A}$ remained. The solution in the distillation flask and the precipitate formed therein were saturated by boiling with carbon dioxide. The resulting precipitate was filtered and dried; the resulting mass of the precipitate was 443.68 g. An excess of hydrochloric acid was added to the precipitate. After the reaction, precipitate $\mathbf{B}$ remained, the mass of which, after calcination at $400\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, was 58.88 g.

a) Write equations of all the reactions taking place.

b) What mass of $\ce{CaO}$ is needed to react completely with this ore?

c) Write the reaction equations if the reaction mixture was heated with calcium oxide in a current of air.

d) What is the % of both $\ce{FeS}$ and $\ce{HgS}$ in the ore?

e) Why was the solution boiled while being saturated with carbon dioxide?

problems.title: Carbon monoxide conversion
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Carbon monoxide conversion

Carbon dioxide formed during the combustion of solid fuel takes part in the equilibrium reaction (1) $\ce{C(s) + CO2(g) <=> 2CO(g)}$. The logarithms of the equilibrium constants at 1000 K of the following reactions are given: (2) $\ce{C(s) + 1/2O2(g) <=> CO(g)}$ $\log K_2 = 10.477$ and (3) $\ce{C(s) + O2(g) <=> CO2(g)}$ $\log K_3 = 20.675$.

a) Calculate the equilibrium constant of reaction (1) at 1000 K and 1 atm pressure.

b) Find the content of gases ($\ce{CO2}$, $\ce{CO}$, $\ce{N2}$) in vol. % if the temperature in the furnace is 1000 K. The fuel burns in the air, the composition of which is assumed to be 80% $\ce{N2}$ and 20% $\ce{O2}$.

problems.title: A simple galvanic cell
problems.problem:
Problem 4. A simple galvanic cell

At $20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the standard EMF of the cell $\ce{Pt, H2 | HCl, HgCl2 | Hg}$ is 0.2692 V; at $30\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, it is equal to 0.2660 V. The calomel electrode is the positive pole.

a) Write the total reaction equation of the cell.

b) Determine $\Delta G^\circ$, $\Delta H^\circ$, $\Delta S^\circ$ and the equilibrium constant of the reaction at $25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

problems.title: A funny ketone
problems.problem:
Problem 5. A funny ketone

Compound $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C13H15NO}$) can react with iodine in an alkaline aqueous solution. As a result of the reaction, yellow precipitate $\mathbf{B}$ ($w_\mathrm{I} = 96.70\%$) and acid $\mathbf{C}$ ($\ce{C12H13NO2}$) are formed. Compound $\mathbf{C}$ undergoes hydrolysis giving products $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{E}$ ($\ce{C7H7NO2}$). The original compound $\mathbf{A}$ undergoes hydrolysis giving products $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{F}$. When substance $\mathbf{F}$ reacts with iodine and sodium hydroxide, compounds $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are formed after acidification of the reaction mixture with hydrochloric acid.

Compound $\mathbf{E}$ decomposes if heated with $\ce{NaOH}$. In this case, it is possible to isolate the basic compound $\mathbf{G}$ ($\ce{C6H7N}$). This compound reacts with an aqueous solution of $\ce{Br2}$ to form a precipitate. Compound $\mathbf{D}$ ($\ce{C5H8O}$) does not decolorize the solution of $\ce{KMnO4}$. It does not react with metallic sodium or silver oxide in ammonia. It can be oxidized under harsh conditions to acid $\ce{C5H8O4}$.

Draw the structural formulas of compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{G}$.

problems.title: Sweet toxins
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Sweet toxins

Many marine mollusks contain the toxic substance holothurin, which has the structure $\mathbf{R{-}O{-}TS}$, in which $\mathbf{R}$ is a polycyclic alcohol residue, and $\mathbf{TS}$ is a tetrasaccharide composed of four different monosaccharides $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, and $\mathbf{D}$.

After complete acid hydrolysis, two monosaccharides are readily identifiable by paper chromatography. These monosaccharides are glucose ($\mathbf{A}$) and xylose ($\mathbf{B}$). The molecular mass of saccharide $\mathbf{C}$ is $164\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ and monosaccharide $\mathbf{D}$ is $194\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$. According to the NMR spectrum, monosaccharides $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{D}$ contain one methyl group. Both monosaccharides can be obtained from glucose: monosaccharide $\mathbf{C}$ is obtained by selective reduction; monosaccharide $\mathbf{D}$ is obtained by methylation at the third position.

By partial enzyme hydrolysis of the tetrasaccharide, the oligosaccharides $\mathbf{DA{-}OH}$, $\mathbf{CD{-}OH}$, and $\mathbf{DAB{-}OH}$ can be isolated ($-$OH represents the oligosaccharide's free reducing group).

a) Draw the structural formulas of $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{D}$.

b) Draw the structural formula of a tetrasaccharide, assuming that all monosaccharides are in pyranose form and that all monosaccharides are joined by a $\beta(1\to4)$ glycosidic bond.

The structures of glucose and xylose are as follows:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-1997-6-fig1.png

problems.title: Another white powder in the lab
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Another white powder in the lab

The analysis laboratory received a white crystalline material for analysis. The analyst weighed out two samples of the material. Sample 1, with a mass of 1.084 g, was dissolved in water. As the material dissolved, $26.17\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of gas, having a mass of 37.39 mg, was released. The resulting solution was found to be very acidic. Addition of hydrochloric acid caused a precipitate to form. After the addition of $47.5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ 0.0983 molar $\ce{HCl}$, no more precipitate was formed. The precipitate was recovered, dried, and weighed. The mass of the precipitate was 0.6693 g.

Sample 2, with a mass of 1.120 g, was heated to above $300\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. During heating, $324.6\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of gas was collected with a mass of 599.0 mg. After heating, a light-colored metal with a mass of 0.521 g remained. The gas was dissolved in $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of water. Not all the gas dissolved, $54.10\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, with a mass of 77.2 mg, remained. The pH of the solution was found to be 1.015.

a) Determine the compound in the sample with calculations.

b) What reactions took place during the analysis?

problems.title: Analysis of gas mixture
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Analysis of gas mixture

A sample of a compound was heated at $600\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A solid with a mass of 4.51 g remained after heating and $21.48\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of gas was liberated at $600\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The solid contains 21.25% oxygen. After cooling to room temperature, the gas occupies $2.69\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ and has a density of $1.61\ \mathrm{g\,dm^{-3}}$. After passing the gas through an alkaline solution, there remained $1.34\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of a combustible gas having a density of $1.25\ \mathrm{g\,dm^{-3}}$.

a) Determine the compound in the sample.

b) Write all appropriate equations.

problems.title: Recreating a natural biosynthesis in a lab
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Recreating a natural biosynthesis in a lab

$R$-(+)-glycerol aldehyde can be transformed to (−)-malic acid (2-hydroxybutanedioic acid) according to the following scheme. $R$-(+)-glycerol aldehyde was treated with hydrogen cyanide and two isomeric compounds were formed, namely $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$. Those compounds were separated by fractional crystallization. Only isomer $\mathbf{B}$ was used for further transformations. This compound was converted to $\mathbf{C}$ ($\ce{C4H8O5}$) upon hydrolysis and then oxidized by conc. nitric acid to produce compound $\mathbf{D}$ ($\ce{C4H6O6}$). Further, compound $\mathbf{D}$ was treated with phosphorus tribromide, thus, compound $\mathbf{E}$ ($\ce{C4H5BrO5}$) was formed. Finally, compound $\mathbf{E}$ was converted to (−)-malic acid after the reaction of zinc with an acid.

a) Write the equations of all reactions using stereochemical (Fisher projections) formulas.

b) Explain why only one isomer $\mathbf{E}$ was formed from $\mathbf{D}$.

c) How many isomers of $\mathbf{E}$ can be formed starting the synthesis from an isomer $\mathbf{A}$?

problems.title: Lethally spicy
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Lethally spicy

Mustard gas (2,2'-dichloro sulfide) can be used as a chemical weapon via releasing $\ce{HCl}$ in hydrolysis reaction. In comparison, 1,5-dichloropentane is hydrolyzed much more slowly.

a) Write the mechanism of the above-described reaction for both compounds.

b) Which well-known compound might be used to destroy this gas?

c) Write a synthetic pathway to produce the mustard gas.

problems.title: A rapid synthesis of ethane
problems.problem:
Problem 5. A rapid synthesis of ethane

The thermal decomposition of azomethane (compound $\mathbf{A}$) follows the equation:

$$\ce{H3CN=NCH3(g) -> C2H6(g) + N2(g)}$$

The half-life of compound $\mathbf{A}$ at $320.6\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is 9.5 min. The total pressure of the mixture of gases at the temperature of $298.0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ was measured at different time periods:

$$\begin{array}{r|c|c|c|c} t\ [\mathrm{min}] & 10.0 & 21.0 & 35.0 & \infty \\ \hline p\ [\mathrm{Torr}] & 491.9 & 548.0 & 609.7 & 861.6 \end{array}$$

a) Prove that the process is a first-order reaction.

b) Calculate the average value of the rate constant at $298.0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

c) Determine the activation energy of the reaction.

problems.title: pH-dependent titration
problems.problem:
Problem 6. pH-dependent titration

Eriochrome Black T ($\ce{H3Ind}$) is a typical metal ion indicator used in complex-formation titrations with EDTA ($\ce{Na2H2Y}$). This compound contains a sulfonic acid group, which is completely dissociated in water, and two phenolic groups that dissociate only partially ($K_\mathrm{a1} = 5.0\cdot10^{-7}$ and $K_\mathrm{a2} = 2.8\cdot10^{-12}$).

$$\begin{array}{c} \ce{H2O + H2Ind^-}\ \text{(red)} \ce{<=> HInd^{2-}}\ \text{(blue)} \ce{+ H3O+} \\ \ce{H2O + HInd^{2-}}\ \text{(blue)} \ce{<=> Ind^{3-}}\ \text{(orange)} \ce{+ H3O+} \end{array}$$

a) The metal complexes of Eriochrome Black T are generally red. Calculate the minimum pH at which Eriochrome Black T can be used as an indicator in complex-formation titrations (assume that the detectable color change requires a tenfold excess of one or other colored species).

b) Determine the transition range for Eriochrome Black T in titrations of $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$ and $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ at pH 10.0, given that the (thermodynamic) formation constant for $\ce{MgInd^-}$ is $1.0\cdot10^{7}$ and for $\ce{CaInd^-}$ is $2.58\cdot10^{5}$.

$50.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.00500 M $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$ and $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ solutions were both titrated with 0.0100 M EDTA solution at pH 10. Conditional formation constants (Instead of the equilibrium concentration of $\ce{Y^{4-}}$ the total concentration of all forms of EDTA is used) at that pH are $1.72\cdot10^{8}$ for $\ce{MgY^{2-}}$ and $1.75\cdot10^{10}$ for $\ce{CaY^{2-}}$.

c) Calculate the equilibrium concentrations of the metal cations at the equivalence point.

d) Determine the sign of the relative error, connected with assuming that the stoichiometric point is judged to be approached at the first change of color of the solution.

problems.title: Haloalkane redox magic
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Haloalkane redox magic

Compound $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C8H15Cl}$) is a racemate. It does not discolor bromine in carbon tetrachloride or potassium permanganate solution. If $\mathbf{A}$ is treated with zinc and acetic acid and the resulting mixture is separated by chromatography, two fractions, $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{C}$, with identical molecular formulas, are obtained. Fraction $\mathbf{B}$ is a racemate.

The reaction of $\mathbf{A}$ with sodium methoxide ($\ce{CH3ONa}$) in ethanol yields compound $\mathbf{D}$. Hydrogenation of $\mathbf{D}$ over a platinum catalyst gives the product $\mathbf{C}$. Ozonolysis of $\mathbf{D}$ followed by the addition of zinc and water produces the dione $\mathbf{E}$. From compound $\mathbf{E}$, iodoform is formed by reaction with iodine in $\ce{NaOH}$ solution. After isolation of iodoform and acidification, adipic acid (1,4-butanedicarboxylic acid) is obtained.

a) Write the structural formulas of $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$, and $\mathbf{E}$.

b) Show the stereoisomerism of the compounds.

c) Write the reaction equations.

d) Write the reaction mechanism for the preparation of compound $\mathbf{D}$ from compound $\mathbf{A}$.

problems.title: The ones that hide inside potatoes
problems.problem:
Problem 2. The ones that hide inside potatoes

Hydrolysis of starch in dilute aqueous acid solution yields only "sweet" products − saccharides: glucose, maltose, etc. Hydrolysis of 30-40% starch suspension in dilute $\ce{HCl}$ solution at 130-140 °C gives bittersweet saccharide $\mathbf{X}$. Substance $\mathbf{X}$ was separated and purified for analysis. A series of experiments were carried out to identify it.

(1) Hydrolysis of starch in acidic solution. One of the products is glucose.

(2) Reducing properties.

25 mg of substance $\mathbf{X}$ was diluted in $25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.0100 M $\ce{K3[Fe(CN)6]}$ solution, $5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.1 M $\ce{KOH}$ solution was added and the mixture was heated at 100 °C for 15 minutes. The concentration of $\ce{K3[Fe(CN)6]}$ was determined using the iodometry method. $\ce{KI}$ and $\ce{CH3COOH}$ were added; $10.5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.0100 M $\ce{Na2S2O3}$ solution was required to titrate $\ce{I2}$.

(3) Methylation and oxidation.

Substance $\mathbf{X}$ was methylated with excess $\ce{CH3I}$ in the presence of $\ce{Ag2O}$. The product was heated in a 30% nitric acid solution. Two acids were detected in the reaction mixture: 2,3,4-trimethoxy-5-hydroxyadipic acid, $\ce{HOOC-CH(OH)-[CH(OCH3)]3-COOH}$ and 2,3,4,6-tetramethoxy-5-hydroxycaproic acid $\ce{H3COCH2CH(OH)-[CH(OCH3)]3COOH}$.

a) Draw the structure of substance $\mathbf{X}$.

b) Write the reaction equations for the identification of substance $\mathbf{X}$.

problems.title: A way to dissolve silver
problems.problem:
Problem 3. A way to dissolve silver

The potential $E_1$ of the silver electrode was determined in a solution of $\ce{AgNO3}$ with a concentration of 0.0100 M. After that, 0.0170 g of $\ce{NH3}$ was added to $10.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the solution. In the resulting solution, the potential of the Ag electrode was different from $E_1$ by 0.285 V. The temperature of the solution was 25 °C.

$\ce{NH3}$ forms a complex in $\ce{AgNO3}$ solution according to the reaction $\ce{Ag+ + 2NH3 <=> [Ag(NH3)2]+}$. Calculate the equilibrium constant of the above reaction.

problems.title: Hydrazinc
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Hydrazinc

$25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.0160 M $\ce{Zn(NO3)2}$ solution and $75\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.133 M hydrazine solution were mixed. $K_\mathrm{sp}[\ce{Zn(OH)2}] = 1.20\cdot10^{-17}$, $K_\mathrm{b}(\ce{H4N2}) = 1.3\cdot10^{-6}$ (proton addition).

a) Write all the reaction equations and give expressions for the equilibrium constants.

b) Calculate the equilibrium concentration for each component of the solution.

c) Calculate the pH of the solution.

problems.title: Carbon tet
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Carbon tet

2.000 g of unknown metal oxide with an oxygen content of 31.58% was heated at 750 °C in a quartz tube. Gaseous $\ce{CCl4}$ was passed through the tube. The gases exiting the tube were passed through lime water. 1.974 g of a white substance precipitated, which dissolved in a hydrochloric acid solution. A red-purple powder remained in the tube. At a reduced temperature, chlorine was passed through the tube. At a reduced temperature, the solid turned into a gas which, in reaction with solid $\ce{CO2}$, turned into a brown solid with a chlorine content of 73.1%. The reaction of this compound with water produced an acidic solution and a mixture of gases that changed the color of the $\ce{KI}$ solution to brown when passed through it.

a) Write all the reaction equations and support them with calculations.

b) What are the processes involved in the reaction of brown solid with water?

problems.title: A colorful manganese complex
problems.problem:
Problem 6. A colorful manganese complex

$\ce{KSCN}$ solution was added to $\ce{Mn(NO3)2}$ solution and a crystalline substance with a molar mass of $445.8\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ was obtained. The experimentally determined magnetic moment of this compound was equal to $\mu = 6.1$ Bohr magneton. $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$. Write the formula of the obtained substance, draw its structure, and explain what information the value of the magnetic moment provides.

problems.title: Four seasons
problems.problem:
Problem 7. Four seasons

At 500 °C, 8.000 g of substance $\mathbf{B}$ and $2.469\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of gaseous substance $\mathbf{C}$ (20 °C and 740 mm Hg) are formed from salt $\mathbf{A}$ in water vapor. The gas $\mathbf{C}$ reacts completely with the original amount of substance $\mathbf{A}$ in an aqueous solution to form 16.800 g of substance $\mathbf{D}$. When the resulting solution is boiled and then dried, the original amount of substance $\mathbf{A}$ is released.

Determine the compounds $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, and $\mathbf{D}$ (all are water-soluble) and write and prove the reaction of $\mathbf{A}$ with water vapor.

problems.title: Volcanic combustion
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Volcanic combustion

Compound $\mathbf{X}$ is colored and burning. Burning 2.12 g of it produces 0.752 g of green solid compound with a very high melting temperature. Gases arising in this process were passed through the excess of lime water. There was 6.838 g of white precipitate, which dissolved in hydrochloric acid. When $\ce{H2O2}$ is added to lime water, the mass of the precipitate is 7.551 g, and only 19.7% (by mass) of the precipitate dissolves in hydrochloric acid. The relative density of the evolved gas against the air is 1.52.

a) Determine compound $\mathbf{X}$.

b) Write equations of the described reactions

c) What is the color of compound $\mathbf{X}$?

problems.title: A rainbow metal
problems.problem:
Problem 2. A rainbow metal

To 10.00 mg of metal $\mathbf{A}$ was added $10\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of water. A stream of chlorine was passed through the water until $\mathbf{A}$ had dissolved completely and an equilibrium had been established. The obtained solution was evaporated in a vacuum to leave 20.91 mg of yellow crystals of a strong acid $\mathbf{B}$. Acid $\mathbf{B}$ obtained in the first reaction was dissolved in water and neutralized exactly with $22.53\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of alkali with a concentration of 2.253 mM. The essentially colorless solution was diluted to $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, and a reducing agent was added. The solution turned bright red. The addition of any salts causes the solution to gradually turn blue. On standing, the blue solution very slowly deposits 10.00 mg of metal $\mathbf{A}$ and becomes colorless once again.

a) Draw and explain the spatial structure of the anion of acid $\mathbf{B}$.

b) Write all the equations of the mentioned reactions.

c) What kind of compounds are best suited to reduce $\mathbf{B}$ and obtain the red solution?

d) What would be observed if the neutralized solution of $\mathbf{B}$ was not diluted prior to the reduction?

e) Explain the role of salts in the color change of the solution.

Solutions of alkali metal salts of $\mathbf{B}$ are slightly acidic. Acidity decreases considerably if excess chloride is present. Explain this finding and calculate the relevant equilibrium constant.

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline n(\mathbf{B})\ [\mathrm{mmol}] & n(\ce{NaCl})\ [\mathrm{mmol}] & V_\text{sol.}\ [\mathrm{cm^3}] & \mathrm{pH} \\ \hline 1.00 & & 1000 & 3.17 \\ \hline 1.00 & 10.0 & 1000 & 3.57 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

problems.title: Same formula, different compounds
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Same formula, different compounds

Three compounds, $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$, have the formula $\ce{C6H10}$. All three compounds rapidly decolorize bromine in $\ce{CCl4}$. Compound $\mathbf{A}$ gives a precipitate when treated with silver nitrate in ammonia, but compounds $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ do not. Compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ both yield compound $\ce{C6H14}$ when treated with excess hydrogen in the presence of a platinum catalyst. Under these conditions, $\mathbf{C}$ absorbs only 1 mol of hydrogen per 1 mol of $\mathbf{C}$ and gives the product with the formula $\ce{C6H12}$. When $\mathbf{A}$ is oxidized with hot potassium permanganate, and the resulting solution is acidified, the only organic compound that can be isolated is $n$-pentanoic acid. Similar oxidation of $\mathbf{B}$ gives only propanoic acid, and similar treatment of $\mathbf{C}$ gives only 1,6-hexanedicarboxylic acid.

a) Draw the structural formulas of compounds $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$.

b) Write equations of the described reactions.

c) Draw the stereochemical formula of the compound produced in the reaction of $\mathbf{C}$ with $\ce{Br2}$.

problems.title: A breakthrough in surgery
problems.problem:
Problem 4. A breakthrough in surgery

($N$,$N$-diethylamino)ethyl 4-aminobenzoate hydrochloride (novocaine) is used as a local anesthetic. It is commonly obtained from the toluene:

$$\text{Toluene} \rightarrow \ce{C7H7NO2} \rightarrow \ce{C7H7NO4} \rightarrow \ce{C9H9NO4} \rightarrow \ce{C9H11NO4} \rightarrow\ \rightarrow \text{Novocaine}$$

$\ce{C7H7NO2}$ and $\ce{C7H5NO4}$ both have 1 singlet and 2 doublets in the $\ce{^1H}$-NMR spectrum. $\ce{C9H9NO4}$ has 2 doublets, 1 triplet, and 1 quartet and $\ce{C9H11NO4}$ has 1 singlet, 2 doublets, 1 triplet and 1 quartet.

a) Write all reaction equations.

b) Write a mechanism for the last reaction in the presence of a catalytic amount of an alkoxide.

c) Outline the $\ce{^1H}$-NMR spectrum of Novocaine.

d) Name the principal bands in its IR spectrum.

A test reaction for Novocaine includes successive treatment of the sample with an acidified solution of sodium nitrite and 2-naphthol. The reaction is positive when precipitate is formed.

e) Write the reaction equation.

problems.title: A primitive pH meter
problems.problem:
Problem 5. A primitive pH meter

A Voltaic cell is made up of two half-cells consisting of hydrogen electrodes (with $\ce{H2}$ gas at $10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$). One of them is immersed in $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.10 M $\ce{HCl}$ aqueous solution, the second one in $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.10 M $\ce{CH3COOH}$ ($K_\mathrm{a} = 1.75\cdot10^{-5}$) aqueous solution.

a) Calculate the EMF of the Voltaic cell under given conditions.

b) Calculate the EMF of the Voltaic cell when $60\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 0.10 M $\ce{NaOH}$ solution was added to both initial solutions.

c) Calculate the EMF of the Voltaic cell when both initial solutions were diluted 10 times.

d) Calculate the volume (in $\mathrm{cm^3}$) of 0.10 M $\ce{NaOH}$ solution that should be added to the initial $\ce{CH3OOH}$ solution to obtain an EMF of $0.150\ \mathrm{V}$.

problems.title: Nuclear waste with a red flame
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Nuclear waste with a red flame

$\ce{^{90}Sr}$ is one of the most common nuclear wastes from nuclear reactors. The spontaneous radioactive decay of this isotope can be described with the following equations: $\ce{^{90}Sr} = \ce{^{90}Y} + \mathrm{e^-}$ and $\ce{^{90}Y} = \ce{^{90}Zr} + \mathrm{e^-}$ ($T_{1/2} = 64$ hours). For a sample of $\ce{^{90}Sr}$ containing $2.64\cdot10^{10}$ atoms, the absolute disintegration rate was measured as 1238 decays per minute. The final Zr isotope is stable.

a) Calculate the amount of energy (in kJ) that is released during one year if we start with one mole of $\ce{^{90}Sr}$.

b) Calculate the ratio of masses of charcoal and $\ce{^{90}Sr}$ that can give this amount of energy. The heat of combustion for charcoal is $23\ \mathrm{MJ\,kg^{-1}}$. $m(\ce{^{90}Sr}) = 89.907738\ \mathrm{Da}$, $m(\ce{^{90}Y}) = 89.907152\ \mathrm{Da}$, $m(\ce{^{90}Zr}) = 89.904703\ \mathrm{Da}$, $m(\mathrm{e^-}) = 5.4857\cdot10^{-4}$

problems.title: Lead and oxalate
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Lead and oxalate

The solubility product value ($K_\mathrm{sp}$) for $\ce{PbC2O4}$ at $25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $8.50\cdot10^{-10}$, and the standard reduction potential of the $\ce{Pb^{2+}}/\ce{Pb}$ couple is $E_1^\circ = -0.126\ \mathrm{V}$.

a) Calculate the standard potential of the half-reaction: $\ce{PbC2O4(s) + 2e- -> Pb(s) + C2O4^{2-}(aq)}$.

b) Calculate the concentration of $\ce{Pb^{2+}}$ ions in 0.0250 M solution of $\ce{Na2C2O4}$ solution saturated with $\ce{PbC2O4}$.

c) Calculate the voltage of the $\ce{PbC2O4}/\ce{Pb}$ electrode in 0.0250 M solution of $\ce{Na2C2O4}$.

problems.title: NOx conversion of carbon monoxide
problems.problem:
Problem 2. NO$_x$ conversion of carbon monoxide

One of the gaseous reactions taking place in car engines and exhaust systems is $\ce{NO2(g) + CO(g) -> NO(g) + CO2(g)}$. Experimental data for this reaction are the following:

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l|l} \text{Experiments} & \text{Initial }[\ce{NO2}],\ \mathrm{M} & \text{Initial }[\ce{CO}],\ \mathrm{M} & \text{Initial rate, }\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}\,s^{-1}} \\ \hline 1 & 0.10 & 0.10 & 0.0050 \\ \hline 2 & 0.40 & 0.10 & 0.080 \\ \hline 3 & 0.10 & 0.20 & 0.0050 \end{array}$$

a) Determine the rate law.

Three possible mechanisms have been proposed for the given reaction:

$$\begin{array}{llll} \text{i)} & \ce{NO2 + CO -> NO + CO2} & \text{iii)} & \ce{NO2 + NO2 -> N2 + 2O2} \\ \text{ii)} & \ce{NO2 + NO2 -> NO3 + NO} & & \ce{O2 + 2CO -> 2CO2} \\ & \ce{NO3 + CO -> NO2 + CO2} & & \ce{N2 + O2 -> 2NO} \end{array}$$

b) Which mechanism is the most reasonable? What is the rate-determining step?

c) Draw the reaction energy diagram (energy-reaction coordinate) for the actual mechanism.

problems.title: An unknown alloy
problems.problem:
Problem 3. An unknown alloy

1.50 g of metal alloy was pulverized and treated with excess $\ce{NaOH}$ solution. The undissolved residue was filtered, washed with water, and dried. The weight of the obtained product was 0.903 g. 20% solution of $\ce{NH4Cl}$ was added to the filtrate until no more precipitation occurred. The formed precipitate was filtered, washed, dried, and heated. 0.510 g of the white compound was obtained. The oxygen content in this compound is 47.1% (by mass). The Undissolved residue was treated with a hydrochloric acid solution. $112\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of hydrogen gas was formed. The Undissolved residue was separated as previously. Its weight was 0.624 g. This residue was treated with a nitric acid solution. The blue solution was obtained. When the ammonia solution is added to the blue solution, a blue precipitate is formed, which dissolves in excess ammonia. 0.179 g of metallic residue was obtained. The volume of the residue is $9.27\ \mathrm{mm^3}$.

a) Determine the composition of metal alloy.

b) Calculate the amount (in moles) of all metals in the alloy.

c) Write the equations of all the described reactions.

problems.title: Unsafe moonshine
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Unsafe moonshine

Colorless liquid ($\mathbf{A}$) is found in the vessel. Apparently, it is a solution of unknown compounds in the water. The solution is slightly acidic. $100.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of this solution was measured and transferred in the distillation flask. Afterwards, $50\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of 20% $\ce{NaOH}$ solution was added. The distilled solution was collected in the flask that contained 100.0 g 3.00% $\ce{HCl}$ solution. Distillation was carried out until the volume of the solution in the collection flask was $150\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. $20.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the obtained solution was measured and titrated with 0.100 M $\ce{KOH}$ solution in the presence of methyl orange. $6.96\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of titrant was used.

To the $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of solution ($\mathbf{A}$), 15 g zinc was added and the procedures mentioned above were repeated. Distillation was interrupted when the volume of distillate was $150\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. In this case, $5.62\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ 0.100 M $\ce{NaOH}$ solution was used for titration.

To the $20.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the solution ($\mathbf{A}$), an excess of $\ce{BaCl2}$ solution was added. 0.467 g of white precipitate was formed. This precipitate did not dissolve in hydrochloric acid. This reaction was repeated, but instead of $\ce{BaCl2}$, a solution of $\ce{Ba(NO3)2}$ was taken. The weight of the obtained precipitate was the same (0.467 g).

To the small volume of solution ($\mathbf{A}$), sulfuric acid and $\ce{FeSO4}$ solution were added. By adding $\ce{KSCN}$, the solution became red. The presence of the other ions was not detected.

a) Determine the qualitative and quantitative composition of solution ($\mathbf{A}$).

b) Write equations of the described reactions.

problems.title: Urushi lacquer is expensive for a reason
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Urushi lacquer is expensive for a reason

Urushiols are the irritants in poison ivy and poison oak that give you rashes and make you itch upon exposure. Use the following information to determine the structure of urushiol $\ce{C21H34O2}$, one of the members of a family of unpleasant compounds.

Urushiol was methylated and, after ozonolysis, gave two compounds as shown in the scheme:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2001-5-fig1.png

Synthesis of aldehyde $\mathbf{A}$ is achieved via the following scheme: treatment of methoxybenzene with fuming sulfuric acid and subsequent nitration with concentrated nitric acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid afforded compound $\mathbf{B}$ ($\ce{C7H7NSO6}$). Heating of $\mathbf{B}$ in dilute aqueous acid gave compound $\mathbf{C}$ ($\ce{C7H7NO3}$). Treatment of $\mathbf{C}$ with $\ce{Zn}$ in $\ce{HCl}$ and subsequent addition of $\ce{NaNO2}$ in acidic media and heating gave compound $\mathbf{D}$ ($\ce{C7H8O2}$). The reaction of $\mathbf{D}$ with $\ce{CO2}$ and $\ce{KHCO3}$ at high pressure (The Kolbe reaction) led to compound $\mathbf{E}$ ($\ce{C8H8O4}$), which with $\ce{CH3I}$ and $\ce{NaOH}$ gave compound $\mathbf{F}$ ($\ce{C9H10O4}$). Reduction of $\mathbf{F}$ with $\ce{LiAlH4}$ and subsequent oxidation with $\ce{MnO2}$ gave compound $\mathbf{G}$ ($\ce{C9H10O3}$). Wittig reaction of $\mathbf{G}$ with $\ce{C6H5CH2O(CH2)6CH=P(C6H5)3}$ gives unsaturated compound $\mathbf{H}$ ($\ce{C23H30O3}$). Hydrogenation of $\mathbf{H}$ with hydrogen on $\ce{Pd}$ gave compound $\mathbf{I}$ ($\ce{C16H26O3}$) which upon oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate afforded aldehyde $\mathbf{A}$.

Draw the structural formula of urushiol and compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{I}$.

problems.title: Protein sequencing
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Protein sequencing

Edman degradation is the most important method for the identification of N-terminal amino acids of peptides and proteins. This method is based on the reaction of an uncharged N-terminal amino group with phenyl isothiocyanate. The addition product $\mathbf{I}$ is formed which, under mildly acidic conditions, decomposes into cyclic compound $\mathbf{II}$ and peptide or protein molecule shortened by one amino acid. The overall reaction equation is presented below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2001-6-fig1.png

a) Draw the structural formula of the intermediate product $\mathbf{I}$.

b) Write the structural formula of cyclic compound $\mathbf{II}$ derived from terminal glycine.

c) Propose a possible mechanism for the transformation of $\mathbf{I}$ into the final product.

d) Write other methods for the identification of terminal amino acids.

Bradykinin is a nonapeptide released by blood plasma globulins. It is a very potent pain-causing agent. Complete acidic hydrolysis of 1 mol of bradykinin gives 3 moles of Pro, 2 moles of Arg, 2 moles of Phe, and also Gly and Ser (1 mole each). Both N- and C-terminals of bradykinin are residues of arginine (Arg). Partial hydrolysis of this nonapeptide gives a mixture of di- and tripeptides:

Phe–Ser, Pro–Gly–Phe, Pro–Pro, Ser–Pro–Phe, Phe–Arg, Arg–Pro

e) Write the amino acid sequence of bradykinin.

problems.title: A pink element
problems.problem:
Problem 1. A pink element

A stream of heated $\ce{Cl2}$ was passed through 0.300 g of element $\mathbf{A}$. On cooling with ice, 1.06 g of pink solid $\mathbf{B}$ was collected in a receiver flask. Compound $\mathbf{B}$ was heated in a stream of $\ce{N2}$, and then the resulting gases were passed through a $\ce{KI}$ solution, which darkened in the process. The solution was then triturated with 0.120 M $\ce{Na2S2O3}$ solution. The white compound $\mathbf{C}$, obtained by heating compound $\mathbf{B}$, was dissolved in a small amount of water. The solution was distilled to dryness, and solid $\mathbf{D}$ was obtained. The distillate was diluted with water to $150.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ (solution of $\mathbf{E}$). $20.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of solution of $\mathbf{E}$ was titrated with 0.100 M $\ce{NaOH}$ solution. Compound $\mathbf{D}$ was heated above $400\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and 0.403 g of white solid $\mathbf{F}$ was obtained. Substance $\mathbf{F}$ was heated in a stream of $\ce{H2}$, and 0.300 g of the initial compound $\mathbf{A}$ was obtained.

a) Write chemical formulas of the compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{F}$.

b) Write all the equations of the reactions.

c) Calculate the volume of $\ce{Na2S2O3}$ solution used for the titration.

d) Calculate the volume of $\ce{NaOH}$ solution used to titrate $20.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of solution $\mathbf{E}$.

e) Why should compound $\mathbf{B}$ be heated in a stream of $\ce{N2}$? What can be used instead of nitrogen?

problems.title: The first step to fertilizers
problems.problem:
Problem 2. The first step to fertilizers

The following reaction is of great practical value: $\ce{N2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2NO(g)}$

a) Determine thermodynamic characteristics for this reaction: $\Delta H_\mathrm{r}^\circ$, $\Delta G_\mathrm{r}^\circ$, $\Delta S_\mathrm{r}^\circ$ if standard values of enthalpy and Gibbs energy for the reaction of $\ce{NO}$ formation are $\Delta H_\mathrm{f}^\circ = 91.25\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\Delta G_\mathrm{f}^\circ = 87.58\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.

b) Write the equation for the dependence of $\Delta G_\mathrm{r}^\circ$ on temperature $T$ assuming that $\Delta H_\mathrm{r}^\circ$ and $\Delta S_\mathrm{r}^\circ$ do not depend on temperature.

c) Estimate the temperature at which air (78% $\ce{N2}$ and 21% $\ce{O2}$) in a closed vessel will contain 0.1% of $\ce{NO}$ by volume at equilibrium.

$\ce{NO}$ is a chemically active compound that is readily oxidized by oxygen and halogens. Assume that the reaction of $\ce{NO}$ with bromine proceeds in 2 steps: i) $\ce{NO + Br2 <=> NOBr2}$ and ii) $\ce{NOBr2 + NO -> 2NOBr}$, where the final one is the rate-limiting step.

d) Write the kinetic equation for the overall reaction of $\ce{NOBr}$ formation.

problems.title: Logic and kinetics
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Logic and kinetics

The enzyme catalyzes the following reaction: $\ce{S -> P}$, where S is the substrate and P is the corresponding product. The reaction rate at different substrate concentrations was measured:

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l|l|l|l} \# & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline [\mathrm{S}],\ \mathrm{M} & 1.0\cdot10^{-2} & 1.0\cdot10^{-3} & 1.0\cdot10^{-4} & 7.5\cdot10^{-5} & 6.25\cdot10^{-6} \\ \hline v_0,\ \mathrm{\mu M\,min^{-1}} & 75.0 & 74.9 & 60.0 & 25.25 & 15.0 \end{array}$$

a) Calculate $v_\mathrm{max}$ and $K_\mathrm{m}$ using only logic and the Michaelis–Menten equation.

b) Calculate the $v_0$ value at substrate concentrations of $2.5\cdot10^{-5}$ and $5\cdot10^{-5}$ M.

c) Calculate the $v_0$ value at a substrate concentration of 0.02 M.

The concentration of the enzyme was increased by a factor of 2.

d) Determine the value of $v_0$ if the substrate concentration is $1\cdot10^{-4}$ M.

e) Calculate the concentration of the product after 3 minutes in the initial concentration of substrate is 0.04 M.

problems.title: Professional burette applications
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Professional burette applications

An analytical lab received a sample of some crystalline compound $\mathbf{X}$ of constant composition for analysis. The laboratory assistant was very experienced in titration, but first of all, he dissolved some part of the sample in water and performed some qualitative trials. He found that the solution of potassium thiocyanate turned red after the addition of some drops of yellow solution $\mathbf{X}$. Also, when the solution of sample $\mathbf{X}$ was mixed with ferrous sulfate and concentrated sulfuric acid was allowed to run slowly down the inside wall of the test tube, a characteristic brown ring appeared at the interface between the two liquids. After that, the lab assistant turned to titration techniques.

1.00 g of sample $\mathbf{X}$ was dissolved in $20.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of water and a small excess of $\ce{TiCl3}$ solution was added. Titration of that mixture required $23.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of titrant $\mathbf{A}$. Titrant $\mathbf{A}$ was prepared by dissolving ceric(IV) sulfate in water. During standardization, $28.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of titrant $\mathbf{A}$ was required to titrate a standard solution prepared by dissolving 0.189 g of $\ce{H2C2O4.H2O}$ in water.

As the obtained information was insufficient, the laboratory assistant prepared a solution of titrant $\mathbf{B}$ (Fischer reagent). He dissolved crystalline iodine in pyridine, then passed $\ce{SO2}$ gas through this solution until the desired mass increase occurred. After that, he diluted the solution with methanol till the desired volume (assume that the solution was prepared using equimolar amounts of iodine and sulfur dioxide). 0.150 g of sample $\mathbf{X}$ was suspended in $5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of methanol and this mixture was rapidly titrated with $8.50\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of titrant $\mathbf{B}$ (assume that titrant reacts with analyte in ratio 1 : 1 and cation does not interfere in reaction). During standardization, $3.40\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of titrant $\mathbf{B}$ was required to titrate a standard solution prepared by dissolving 0.1 g of $\ce{KNaC4H4O6.4H2O}$ in methanol.

a) What ions does the aqueous solution of sample $\mathbf{X}$ contain?

b) Write the equations of standardizations of i) titrant $\mathbf{A}$ and ii) titrant $\mathbf{B}$.

c) Write the equations for the analysis of sample $\mathbf{X}$ using two different titrations.

d) Determine the composition of sample $\mathbf{X}$.

e) What can be the main application of Fischer titration?

f) Is it possible to titrate aldehydes or ketones using Fischer titration in this way?

problems.title: Chemistry of essential oils
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Chemistry of essential oils

Terpenes are compounds with a carbon skeleton consisting of isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) units that are linked in a head-to-tail fashion. They are often found in nature and give a characteristic aroma to many essential oils. Geraniol and nerol are also classified as steroids. These compounds are stereoisomers of a primary alcohol with two double bonds in the molecule. Geraniol is found in geranium oil, and nerol is found in nerol oil and bergamot oil. In the presence of acid, geraniol cyclizes to form α-terpineol, but nerol cyclizes much more rapidly. In the Figure, the carbon skeleton of the precursor alcohols is shown in bold.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2002-5-fig1.png

a) Draw the structural formulas of geraniol and nerol.

b) What feature of the structure accounts for the rapid cyclization of nerol?

α-Terpineol, when dehydrated, forms terpinolene, which is found in the oil of Monteiro cypress.

c) Depict the most probable structure of terpinolene.

In the presence of acid, terpinolene isomerizes to form three isomeric monocyclic dienes called terpinenes. Of these, α-terpinene is the primary product. It is found naturally in marjoram, cardamom, and coriander oil. Only α-terpinene is capable of a good Diels-Alder reaction. However, when treated with excess hydrogen chloride at low temperatures, all three terpinenes form the same addition product.

d) Draw the structural formula of α-terpinene.

e) Draw the structural formula of the Diels-Alder product with maleic anhydride.

f) Draw the structural formulas of the two remaining terpinenes.

g) Draw the structural formulas of the reaction products of terpinenes with excess hydrogen chloride. Draw all possible stereoisomers of this compound.

problems.title: Spectroscopy on steroids
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Spectroscopy on steroids

Steroids are biological regulators in the human body. For example, they control sexual development and fertility. Among the most common steroids, cholesterol is present in almost all human and animal tissues. In steroids, the four cycles are condensed into the tetracyclic structure below. The junctions of the cycles are usually in transposition. The four cycles are labeled A, B, C, and D, and the carbon atoms are numbered according to a steroid-specific scheme. Many steroids have methyl groups at C10 and C13 and oxygen at NW. Bonds to groups above the plane of the steroid molecule are indicated in bold and those below the plane are indicated by dashed lines.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2002-6-fig1.png

a) Alternative wording: Draw the structural formula of the steroid above, indicating the conformations of six-membered cycles.

b) Label the chiral atoms in this structure.

c) Calculate the number of diastereomers of this molecule.

Cholesterol is a steroid in which R = OH, $\mathrm{R^1} = \ce{CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH2CH(CH3)2}$, $\mathrm{R^2} = \mathrm{R^3} = \mathrm{H}$, and there is a double bond between the 5 and 6 carbon atoms. This steroid is responsible for many circulatory diseases due to the fact that it precipitates in the arteries, causing arteriosclerosis and heart disease.

d) Draw the structural formula of cholesterol and identify the configuration of the chiral atoms using ($R$,$S$)-designations.

Under the action of bacteria in the human digestive tract, cholesterol is converted to coprostanol. Use the following information to determine the structure of coprostanol. When treated with a Cr(VI) reagent, coprostanol forms compound $\mathbf{A}$ (IR: $1710\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$; UV: $\lambda_\mathrm{max}(\varepsilon) = 281$). Reaction of cholesterol with $\ce{H2}$ over Pt gives compound $\mathbf{B}$, the stereoisomer of coprostanol. Treatment of $\mathbf{B}$ with a Cr(VI) reagent gives compound $\mathbf{C}$, which has a UV signal very similar to that of compound $\mathbf{A}$ (UV: $\lambda_\mathrm{max}(\varepsilon) = 258$) and is, therefore, the stereoisomer of $\mathbf{A}$. Careful addition of Cr(VI) reagent to cholesterol gives $\mathbf{D}$ (UV: $\lambda_\mathrm{max}(\varepsilon) = 286$). Catalytic hydrogenation of $\mathbf{D}$ over Pt also gives $\mathbf{C}$.

e) Draw structural formulas of compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$. Label the stereochemistry of the atoms involved in the transformations using suitable steroid skeleton designations.

Cholesterol is the precursor to bile acids in the human body. Bile acids are formed in the liver as part of the fluid going into the duodenum to facilitate emulsification, digestion, and absorption of fats. An example is cholic acid (R = OH. $\mathrm{R^1} = \ce{CH(CH3)CH2CH2COOH}$, $\mathrm{R^2} = \mathrm{R^2} = \mathrm{OH}$), in which the articulation of cycles A and B is cis. This acid has surface-active properties.

f) Draw its conformational formula and a diagram showing the formation of micelles of cholic acid in aqueous solution.

Steroid synthesis in the laboratory is carried out using the Robinson annulation method. This reaction between enolates ketones and α,β-unsaturated compounds is followed by intramolecular aldol condensation.

g) Suggest a scheme for the synthesis of the steroid indicated herein from a bicyclic ketone using one or more Robinson annulations and suitable components:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2002-6-fig2.png

h) Write the mechanism of the first step of the synthesis.

problems.title: Packing of peas and lupine
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Packing of peas and lupine

a) Calculate the layer’s thickness of 1 mol of peas (6 mm in diameter), covering the entire surface of the Earth ($5.10\cdot10^{8}\ \mathrm{km^2}$) in the FCC arrangement. Assume that the surface is flat.

b) Choose the correct answer that describes what would happen if these peas were mixed with 1 mol of lupine (2 mm in diameter). Fill in the gaps in your answer.

• With the particle size ratio smaller than 0.414, the FCC arrangement would transform into the … arrangement and the layer’s thickness would be … m.
• Lupine would fit into the … holes of the FCC arrangement of peas, which can accommodate spherical particles with a diameter up to … mm. The layer’s thickness would not change.
• Lupine would occupy the … holes of the FCC arrangement, and it would expand slightly to increase the layer’s thickness to … m.
• Lupine cannot fit into any holes of the FCC arrangement. It would form an independent layer on top of peas. The total thickness of both layers would be … m.
• Lupine would fit easily and indiscriminately into both … and … holes of the FCC arrangement. The layer’s thickness would not change.

problems.title: Nitrogen hydrides
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Nitrogen hydrides

Nitrogen forms more than 20 binary compounds with hydrogen. The most important and well-known are ammonia $\ce{NH3}$, hydrazine $\ce{N2H4}$, hydrogen azide (hydrazoic acid) $\ce{HN3}$ (a non-cyclic molecule), and cyclotriazene $\ce{HN3}$.

Hydrazine $\ce{N2H4}$ is used as a rocket fuel. The oxidation of hydrazine is strongly exothermic:

problems.title: Polonium
problems.problem:

In 1898, Pierre and Marie Curie discovered a new chemical element, polonium, in uranium tar ore (Bohemia, Joachimsthal). One ton of this ore contains 0.14 grams of $\ce{^{226}Ra}$ ($T_{1/2} = 1580$ years). $m(\ce{^4He}) = 4.00273\ \mathrm{Da}$, $m(\beta) = 0.00055\ \mathrm{Da}$, $m(\ce{^{226}Ra}) = 226.02540\ \mathrm{Da}$, $m(\ce{^{210}Po}) = 209.98286\ \mathrm{Da}$

problems.title: Slow reaction

An equilibrium is established in a solution of hydrogen iodide at the silver electrode, which can be expressed by the equations: (i) $\ce{Ag(s) <=> Ag+(aq) + e-}$ ($E^\circ = 0.799\ \mathrm{V}$) and $\ce{Ag+(aq) + I-(aq) <=> AgI(s)}$ or using the total equation (ii) $\ce{Ag(s) + I-(aq) <=> AgI(s) + e-}$ ($E^\circ = -0.152\ \mathrm{V}$).

problems.title: Selenic acid
problems.problem:

1.29 g of crystalline selenic acid $\ce{H2SeO3}$ ($\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a1} = 2.62$, $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a2} = 8.32$) was transferred into a measuring flask and distilled water was added up to $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ mark. problems.title: Tropinic acid
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Tropinic acid

Tropinic acid, $\ce{C8H13O4N}$, is a degradation product of atropine, an alkaloid of the deadly cherry Atropa belladonna. Tropinic acid does not react with cold dilute $\ce{KMnO4}$ solution, $\ce{Br2}/\ce{CCl4}$ solution, and benzenesulfonyl chloride. Complete methylation gives the following results:

• i) Tropinic acid + $\ce{CH3I}$ → $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C9H16O4NI}$)
• ii) $\mathbf{A}$ + $\ce{Ag2O}$ → $\mathbf{B}$ ($\ce{C9H15O9N}$)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2003-6-fig1.png

Tropinic acid is formed by oxidation of tropinone with $\ce{CrO3}$. Reduction of tropinone gives tropine and pseudotropine (both $\ce{C8H15ON}$). When heated with base, tropine is converted to pseudotropine.

a) Draw the structural formulas of tropinic acid and compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$.

problems.title: European Union
problems.problem:
Problem 1. European Union

Two chemists received for analysis two samples of a metal ($\rho = 5.245\ \mathrm{g\cdot cm^{-3}}$) with equal mass. Both chemists used X-ray analysis to determine that the metal crystallized in the BCC arrangement with the elementary cell edge length of 4.582 Å.

The more careless chemist left the sample in the air, where its surface quickly lost metallic shine. When he crushed the sample and put it into a beaker with water, a vigorous reaction gave a white precipitate. The obtained solution was strongly basic. The solution containing the precipitate was acidified with hydrochloric acid and carefully evaporated to obtain 363.7 mg of colorless crystals. Sulfur(IV) oxychloride was added to the crystals and refluxed until the evolution of gases had ceased to give 340.0 mg of white deliquescent crystals. Their IR spectrum was obtained at low temperatures, in high dilution, in the matrix of an inert gas, and displayed four bands. The compound was put into a beaker and dissolved in water. Dilute sulfuric acid was added to the solution until no more precipitate formed. 166.9 mg of colorless crystals were obtained. On heating, the mass of the crystals reduced to 134.2 mg and did not change anymore.

The other chemist never liked to go to the beaten path. So, he dissolved his sample in liquid ammonia to obtain, under an inert atmosphere, a blue solution. As he added ammonium chloride to the solution, the solution became colorless, a gas evolved, and some precipitate formed. The precipitate was gently heated in vacuo to yield 293.3 mg of a white crystalline solid. Its IR spectrum displayed three bands. The compound was put into a beaker and dissolved in water. Dilute sulfuric acid was added to the solution until no more precipitate formed. Some excess acid was added, and the solution was set aside to ensure complete precipitation. Yet, contrary to expectations, the mass of the colorless, crystalline precipitate significantly decreased on standing. By pure coincidence, the second chemist also obtained 166.9 mg of precipitate. On heating, the mass of the precipitate reduced further to 134.2 mg and did not change anymore.

a) Using the X-ray data, determine the analyzed metal.

b) Draw structural formulas for both compounds analyzed by IR spectroscopy. Identify vibrations corresponding to the observed bands.

c) Write equations for all the mentioned reactions.

problems.title: After the fever is gone
problems.problem:

• ii) $-38.5^\circ$
