problems.title: Pharaoh's Compliment
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Pharaoh's Compliment

To the cobalt(II) chloride solution, a white solid $\mathbf{A}$ (18.1% C, 7.52% H, and 53.3% Cl), $\ce{NaOH}$ and 30% $\ce{H2O2}$ were added separately. Orange compound $\mathbf{B}$ (19.8% C, 7.16% H, and 29.3% Cl) was obtained. In small amounts, concentrated ammonia and excess aqueous formaldehyde were added to the solution of $\mathbf{B}$ at pH 10, and a yellow solid $\mathbf{C}$ (31.9% C, 6.65% H, and 23.6% Cl) was isolated. $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ NMR spectra show one signal for $\mathbf{A}$ (43 ppm) and $\mathbf{B}$ (45 ppm) and two signals of equal intensity for C (54 and 67 ppm). $^{1}\mathrm{H}$ NMR spectra in $\ce{D2O}$ show a singlet for $\mathbf{A}$ (2.65 ppm) and a broad singlet for $\mathbf{B}$ (2.85 ppm).

a) Identify compounds $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$.

b) $\mathbf{B}$ is an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers: $\mathbf{B1}$ and $\mathbf{B2}$. Draw structural formulas for $\mathbf{B1}$ and $\mathbf{B2}$. Propose how they can be isolated separately.

c) Compound $\mathbf{C}$ was given the trivial name sepulchrate ("sepulchrum" means "grave or sarcophagus" in Latin). Write a structural formula for $\mathbf{C}$ and propose the reaction $\mathbf{B} \rightarrow \mathbf{C}$ mechanism.

problems.title: Chemical equilibrium
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Chemical equilibrium

The vessel with a volume of $120\underline{0}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ was vacuumed and filled with nitrogen monoxide up to pressure 180.0 mm Hg at 297 K. Then the gas was frozen, and 720.0 mg bromine was added to the vessel. The temperature was raised to 335 K. After the equilibrium was reached, the pressure in the vessel was 230.0 mm Hg.

a) Write the equation for the chemical reaction.

b) Calculate the equilibrium constant $K_\mathrm{p}$ for the nitrosyl bromide decomposition (the vessel volume does not change with the temperature).

c) How does the pressure influence the equilibrium state?

d) Calculate the amount of nitrogen oxide moles in the equilibrium mixture.

problems.title: Electrolysis
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Electrolysis

The aqueous solution containing ethanoic acid and sodium ethanoate was electrolyzed. The gases deliberated on Pt-electrodes were collected and purged through a concentrated $\ce{KOH}$ solution. It was established that during the electrolysis at STP, the mass of the $\ce{KOH}$ solution was increased by 5.213 g.

a) Write the equations for electrode reactions.

b) Calculate the amounts ($\mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}}$) of gases evolved at the anode and reacting and not reacting with $\ce{KOH}$ solution. The relative density of non-reacting gas against hydrogen is 15.0.

c) Calculate the consumed electrical energy (A h) if the yield of anodic reaction products by current was 100%.

d) What was the electrolysis duration if the current was 706 mA? Calculate the mass of Cu deposited in a copper coulometer serially connected with an electrolyzer.

e) Calculate the equilibrium potential when the ratio of ethanate concentrations is 1 : 3 and the hydrogen partial solution is $1.0\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$. $K_\mathrm{a}(\ce{CH3COOH}) = 1.85\cdot10^{-5}$.

problems.title: Blue nitrogen
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Blue nitrogen

Dinitrogen trioxide $\ce{N2O3}$ is an unstable compound that exists in both molecular and ionic forms. On heating, it breaks down into more stable compounds.

a) Write the empirical formulas for the ions that can exist in solid $\ce{N2O3}$.

b) Write the chemical equation for the decomposition of $\ce{N2O3}$.

Dinitrogen trioxide gives an acidic solution when dissolved in water. After careful investigation, it was found that two isomeric compounds were present in the solution.

c) Draw the Lewis structures of the two compounds formed in the reaction of $\ce{N2O3}$ with water. Show the distribution of all valence electrons. Write the formal charges of the atoms if they are not equal to zero. Write the assumed valence angles in Lewis structures.

A solution of compound $\mathbf{A}$ was prepared by dissolving an unknown amount of $\ce{N2O3}$ in water. When the solution of compound $\mathbf{A}$ was treated with a solution of $\ce{FeSO4}$ of equal volume (acidified with sulfuric acid), $n_1$ moles of gas $\mathbf{B}$ were formed. Then, an excess acidified KI solution was added to the same solution. This produced $n_2$ moles of gas $\mathbf{B}$ and a certain amount of a dark-colored substance $\mathbf{C}$ (assume that $\mathbf{C}$ is completely insoluble).

d) Write the equation of the reaction between $\ce{N2O3}$ and water and the equations of all the reactions that occur when substance $\mathbf{A}$ reacts with $\ce{FeSO4}$ and excess acidified KI solution.

e) At room temperature, gas $\mathbf{B}$ is paramagnetic. At very low temperatures, it is diamagnetic. Show schematically what happens to gas $\mathbf{B}$ at low temperatures.

When $n_2$ moles of compound $\mathbf{B}$ react with hot graphite, a mixture of non-flammable gases is formed. If this mixture reacts with a saturated $\ce{Ca(OH)2}$ solution, an insoluble compound $\mathbf{D}$ is formed. Compound $\mathbf{D}$ has a mass 3.00 times smaller than that of compound $\mathbf{C}$.

f) Calculate the ratio of the molar concentrations of $\ce{FeSO4}$ and $\mathbf{A}$ in the starting solution.

g) $0.10\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of gas $\mathbf{B}$ ($100.0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $1.00\ \mathrm{atm}$) was reacted with chlorine $\ce{Cl2}$. The product of this reaction was dissolved in water to give a $1.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ solution. What is the degree of dissociation of the oxygen-containing acid in this solution? ($K_\mathrm{a} = 7.1\cdot10^{-4}$)

problems.title: Display of complex chemicals
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Display of complex chemicals

Complex $\mathbf{X}$ has been studied a lot recently because of its unusual physical properties which are generally only characteristic of organic compounds. Compounds with such properties are produced to the tune of several billion dollars per year. Even now, you can see such a substance in front of you. Compound $\mathbf{X}$ is usually obtained from complex compound $\mathbf{Y}$ by a ligand exchange reaction.

Compound $\mathbf{Y}$ is synthesized directly from metal $\mathbf{Z}$ in a reaction with a ligand. Compound $\mathbf{Y}$ contains 36.34% of metal $\mathbf{Z}$.

a) Identify the metal $\mathbf{Z}$.

b) Write the molecular formula of compound $\mathbf{Y}$. Draw its structure and show the metal hybridization.

In order to carry out the ligand exchange reaction, compound $\mathbf{Y}$ is treated with hexanoic acid. This produces a gas and yields compound $\mathbf{X}$, which contains 29.41% of metal $\mathbf{Z}$. If 2.00 g of compound $\mathbf{X}$ is dissolved in 100 g of benzene, the melting point of benzene is reduced by $0.157\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (the cryoscopic constant of benzene is $5.12\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$). Compound $\mathbf{X}$ is diamagnetic and has no geometric isomers. If racemic 2-deuterohexanoic acid is used to prepare compound $\mathbf{X}$, four compounds are obtained, two of which can be resolved to enantiomers.

c) Write the molecular formula of compound $\mathbf{X}$.

d) Choose the correct answer explaining diamagneetism of compound $\mathbf{X}$.

• $\mathbf{X}$ has an even number of electrons.
• The ligands cause the $d$-orbitals of the metal to undergo energy splitting, resulting in a low spin complex.
• A covalent bond is formed between the metal atoms.
• $\mathbf{X}$ is unstable due to the repulsion of non-bonding d electron pairs of metal atoms.

e) Based on the given data, write realistic structures for compound $\mathbf{X}$ and its analogues obtained in the reaction with deuterated hexanoic acid. Explain which orbitals are involved in which bond formation.

The unusual properties of compound $\mathbf{X}$ are determined by the interaction of its molecules, resulting in a ladder-like structure. The strongest evidence for these properties comes from differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) data, shown in the graph below. This graph shows the dependence between the heat absorbed by the sample and the temperature.

f) Write the processes corresponding to the maxima in the DSC graph. What are the compounds with such properties called?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-2-fig1.png

problems.title: A cycle of additions
problems.problem:
Problem 3. A cycle of additions

Cycloadditions are very common in organic synthesis. The most important of these is the Diels–Alder reaction:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-3-fig1.png

The reaction between cyclopentadiene $\mathbf{A}$ and methyl methacrylate $\mathbf{B}$ gives a mixture of isomers of compound $\mathbf{C}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-3-fig2.png

a) Draw all the isomers (including stereoisomers) of compound $\mathbf{C}$ that are formed in this reaction.

b) Mark all chiral centers with an asterisk and label each center according to the $R/S$ nomenclature.

c) Indicate which isomers of compound $\mathbf{C}$ are enantiomers and which are diastereomers.

Cyclopentadiene is involved in the following reaction:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-3-fig3.png

Treatment of compound $\mathbf{G}$ with ozone and subsequent hydrolysis yields compound $\mathbf{I}$. Ozonolysis of compound $\mathbf{H}$ yields compound $\mathbf{J}$. Heating compound $\mathbf{I}$ in an acidic medium yields compound $\mathbf{K}$. Analysis of compound $\mathbf{I}$ showed that it is a mixture of two enantiomers.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-3-fig4.png

d) Draw the structures of compounds $\mathbf{G}$, $\mathbf{H}$, $\mathbf{I}$, and $\mathbf{J}$.

e) How many chiral centers are there in compounds $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{J}$?

f) How many stereoisomers are there for compound $\mathbf{J}$?

g) Write the mechanism of the reaction $\mathbf{D} \rightarrow \mathbf{G} + \mathbf{H}$

problems.title: A greener soap for polymers
problems.problem:
Problem 4. A greener soap for polymers

As environmental requirements become more stringent, a new type of surfactant is used in emulsion polymerization to replace the well-known sodium alkyl sulfate. These new surfactants have a double bond that allows them to participate in the polymerization reaction and bind irreversibly to polymer particles. As a result, only a small amount of surfactant is consumed and does not end up in wastewater. Surfactant derivatives of ($Z$)-but-2-enoic acid (maleic acid) belong to such a class of compounds.

Surfactant $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C16H28NO3}$) is synthesized by the reaction of maleic anhydride with dodecylamine. Compound $\mathbf{A}$ has very low solubility in water, but its solubility increases with the addition of alkali, resulting in a good surfactant.

a) Write the equations of the reactions involved.

Compound $\mathbf{A}$ can subsequently be used in the synthesis of various surfactants. The synthesis starts with the cyclization of compound $\mathbf{A}$, resulting in compound $\mathbf{B}$, which has two stereoisomers.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-4-fig1.png

b) Draw the structural formulae of these isomers and write the corresponding stereochemical descriptors.

c) Which isomer (if any) would be dominant under equilibrium conditions? Indicate the reason for your choice.

The equilibrium between the isomers in the solution is achieved rapidly. Below is a fragment of the $^1$H NMR spectrum of compound $\mathbf{B}$ with signals corresponding to the double bond protons, and the table shows the relative intensities of the signals.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2005-4-fig2.png

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc|ccc} T,\ ^\circ\mathrm{C} & & 110\ ^\circ\mathrm{C} & & & 70\ ^\circ\mathrm{C} & \\ \hline \text{Signal} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6+7 \\ \hline \text{Rel. int.} & 0.103 & 1.000 & 1.103 & 0.134 & 1.000 & 1.134 \end{array}$$

d) Show the signals corresponding to each isomer (you do not need to determine the signal corresponding to a specific proton).

e) Calculate the equilibrium constant between the two isomers at $70\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $110\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Also, calculate the reaction enthalpy of the transition between the isomers.

Compound $\mathbf{B}$ reacts readily with amines. Commonly, hydrophilic amines are used to produce surfactants, although the reaction also occurs with dodecylamine to give compound $\mathbf{C}$ ($\ce{C28H54N2O2}$). In the $^1$H NMR spectrum, there is only one sharp singlet corresponding to both double-bond protons.

f) Write the reaction equation.

Compound $\mathbf{B}$ isomerizes to compound $\mathbf{D}$, which has the same molecular formula but a significantly lower reactivity than $\mathbf{B}$. It also has only one sharp singlet corresponding to both double-bond protons in the $^1$H NMR spectrum. Compound $\mathbf{B}$ has absorption maxima at $1800\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ and $1700\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ in the IR spectrum, while compound $\mathbf{D}$ does not absorb at a lower wavenumber.

g) Write the structural formula of compound $\mathbf{D}$.

problems.title: An easy way to make a nuke
problems.problem:
Problem 5. An easy way to make a nuke

Part I.

Irradiation of $\ce{^{63}Cu}$ with neutrons produces the radioactive isotope $\ce{^{64}Cu}$, which has a spontaneous half-life of 12,700 hours. 61.0% of $\ce{^{64}Cu}$ atoms decay to $\ce{^{64}Zn}$ and 39.0% of $\ce{^{64}Cu}$ atoms decay to $\ce{^{64}Ni}$.

a) Write the reaction equations by filling in the gaps ($^{0}\tilde{\nu}$ − neutrino; $^{0}\nu$ − antineutrino):

• i) $\ce{^{63}Cu} + {}^{1}\mathrm{n} \rightarrow \ce{^{64}Cu} + \ldots$
• ii) $\ce{^{64}Cu} \rightarrow \ce{^{64}Zn} + \ldots + {}^{0}\tilde{\nu}$
• iii) $\ce{^{64}Cu} \rightarrow \ce{^{64}Ni} + \ldots + {}^{0}\nu$

b) Calculate the percentage of the initial number of $\ce{^{64}Cu}$ atoms that make up the $\ce{^{64}Cu}$, $\ce{^{64}Ni}$, and $\ce{^{64}Zn}$ atoms 25.4 hours after the start of the spontaneous decomposition of $\ce{^{64}Cu}$.

Part II.

Irradiation of $\ce{^{238}U}$ with neutrons produces the radioactive isotope $\ce{^{239}U}$, which spontaneously decays in sequence to produce plutonium-239. The intermediate product of the decay of uranium-239 is $\ce{^{239}Np}$. $\ce{^{239}U}$ has a half-life of 23.5 minutes and $\ce{^{239}Np}$ a half-life of 2.355 days. Plutonium-239 atoms can be considered stable.

c) Finish the equations by filling in the gaps: i) $\ce{^{238}U} + {}^{1}\mathrm{n} \rightarrow \ldots + \gamma$; ii) $\ce{^{239}U} \rightarrow \ldots + {}^{0}\mathrm{e}^{-} + {}^{0}\tilde{\nu}$; iii) $\ce{^{239}Np} \rightarrow \ce{^{239}Pu} + {}^{0}\mathrm{e}^{-} + \ldots$.

A radiochemically pure $\ce{^{239}U}$ sample was prepared to obtain $\ce{^{239}Pu}$.

d) Calculate the time $t_\mathrm{max}$ at which the amount of neptunium in the sample is maximal.

e) Calculate the percentage of $\ce{^{239}U}$, $\ce{^{239}Np}$, and $\ce{^{239}Pu}$ atoms relative to the initial number of $\ce{^{239}U}$ atoms after 170 min.

$$N(\ce{^{239}Np}) = N(\ce{^{239}U})_0\,\frac{k_1}{k_2 - k_1}\left(e^{-k_1 t} - e^{-k_2 t}\right) \qquad \frac{dN(\ce{^{239}Np})}{dt} = N(\ce{^{239}U})_0\,\frac{k_1}{k_2 - k_1}\left(-k_1 e^{-k_1 t} + k_2 e^{-k_2 t}\right)$$

problems.title: A water cycle
problems.problem:
Problem 6. A water cycle

$V_1 = 10.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of water was placed in a container with perfectly elastic walls at a $T_0 = 273.16\ \mathrm{K}$ and an external pressure of $1.000\cdot10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$.

Stage 1. The water was converted to ice at 273.16 K, resulting in an increase in the volume of the container.

Stage 2. The ice was melted and the resulting water was heated to boiling point at $0.900\cdot10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$ until it evaporated. Under these conditions, the volume of the vapor is $V_2$.

Stage 3. The vapor was compressed adiabatically to a volume $V_3 = 10.00\ \mathrm{m^3}$.

Stage 4. The vapor was reversibly isothermally compressed to a volume $V_4 = 5.00\ \mathrm{m^3}$.

Fill in the gaps in the table and make the necessary calculations.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \text{Temperature } T\ [\mathrm{K}] & \text{Volume } V\ [\mathrm{m^3}] & \text{Thermodynamic expansion-compression work } w\ [\mathrm{J}] \\ \hline \text{Stage 1} & 273.16 & 0.01000 & \\ \hline \text{Stage 2} & & & \\ \hline \text{Stage 3} & & 10.00 & \\ \hline \text{Stage 4} & 456.21 & 5.00 & \end{array}$$

The densities of water and ice at $0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ are $0.9987\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ and $0.917\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ respectively. The boiling point of water is $100.00\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (101325 Pa). The enthalpy of water evaporation is $40.665\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, for water vapor $\chi = 1.329$ ($\chi = C_p/C_V$). By convention, the expansion work is considered negative.

problems.title: Versatile purple
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Versatile purple

Element $\mathbf{A}$ can be isolated from its compound $\mathbf{B}$ that occurs naturally in a mixture with Chile saltpeter. Firstly, compound $\mathbf{B}$ is treated with aqueous $\ce{NaSH}$ solution. Then, elemental $\mathbf{A}$ is extracted from the aqueous solution using xylene, which obtains a violet color. Element $\mathbf{A}$ also forms a blue-colored compound with a starch solution.

a) Identify compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$.

b) Write the chemical formula of Chile saltpeter.

c) Write the equation for the treatment of $\mathbf{B}$ with aqueous $\ce{NaSH}$ solution.

Element $\mathbf{A}$ is widely used in medicine. In 1986, after the Chernobyl nuclear power plant disaster, people living near the city of Pripyat were administered medicine containing $\mathbf{A}$.

d) Explain why it is necessary to take medicine containing element $\mathbf{A}$ during the radioactive nuclear fallout.

Element $\mathbf{A}$ is also used in electrical engineering. Many vehicles have some electric details containing small quantities of $\mathbf{A}$ and its tungsten salt.

e) Write the equation of the reversible reaction taking place in the electric detail during its working cycle.

Upon the reaction of element $\mathbf{A}$ with wet red phosphorus, a colorless and toxic gas $\mathbf{C}$ is released. Gaseous compound $\mathbf{C}$ is a strong acid that protolyzes (dissociates into ions) completely in an aqueous medium.

f) Write the equation depicting a reaction between element $\mathbf{A}$ and wet red phosphorus.

g) 12.79 grams of $\mathbf{C}$ was dissolved in $1.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of water. Calculate the pH value of the aqueous solution of compound $\mathbf{C}$.

h) $1.00\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the solution described in g) was diluted with $10.0\ \mathrm{m^3}$ of pure distilled water. Calculate the pH value of the newly obtained solution.

problems.title: Grand Theft Balls
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Grand Theft Balls

To keep the gold ration inviolable, the Schah ordered all the gold to be cast into the shape of spheres, 1 cm in diameter. Being very curious and having found out the richness of the master, the first Vizier decided to appropriate the part of treasures. To put his plan into action, he presented a metal box (75×75×75 cm) and Schah put 578813 gold balls into it in the only possible arrangement (arrangement $\mathbf{I}$). Every day, Schah shook the box and checked whether it made any noise or not, meaning had anyone taken his treasures or not. The first Vizier replaced the balls (arrangement $\mathbf{II}$) and put them in the right arrangement to keep them from thundering so Schah did not find out. So the first Vizier stole a large amount of gold, but it was not enough for him and he replaced the balls once more in such a way that they did not make any sound (arrangement $\mathbf{III}$), having made a fool of his master.

a) Calculate the packing arrangement efficiency of 578813 gold balls in the box. Make a conclusion about the type of arrangement $\mathbf{I}$.

b) Determine the position of atoms in arrangements $\mathbf{I}$–$\mathbf{III}$.

c) Calculate the number of gold balls stolen by the first Vizier at the first and second time.

problems.title: One peak, two downhill pathways
problems.problem:
Problem 3. One peak, two downhill pathways

Consider the following schemes:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2006-3-fig1.png

The $^{1}\mathrm{H}$ NMR spectra of compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$ consist of just one singlet (after the addition of a drop of $\ce{D2O}$), the $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ NMR spectra consist of just two lines. The $^{1}\mathrm{H}$ NMR spectra of compounds $\mathbf{E}$–$\mathbf{G}$ consist of two singlets (after the addition of a drop of $\ce{D2O}$). Combustion of compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{G}$ yields only carbon dioxide and water.

a) Determine compounds that fit this scheme and write all the reaction equations.

b) Arrange compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{X}$ in order of decreasing chemical shift of their only signal in the $^{1}\mathrm{H}$ NMR spectrum.

If the restriction of using 1 mol or 2 mol of the Grignard reagent in the first step of the reaction sequences is removed, one more starting compound fits the first scheme and another starting compound fits the second scheme. Using these compounds leads to the same reaction products $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{D}$, respectively.

c) Determine reaction products $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{D}$.

problems.title: How to set water on fire
problems.problem:
Problem 4. How to set water on fire

The halogens combine with each other to form interhalogen compounds of four stoichiometries: $\mathbf{XY}$, $\mathbf{XY}_3$, $\mathbf{XY}_5$, and $\mathbf{HY}_7$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the heavier halogen. In 1813–1814, J. L. Guy Lussac and H. Davy independently synthesized the first interhalogen compound $\ce{ICl}$.

From the rotational spectrum of a gaseous substance, a rotational constant can be determined. This constant can be expressed in hertz Hz (notation $B$) or in wave numbers (notation $\overline{B}$). The rotational energy of a molecule can be described with the following formula: $E_J = h\cdot B\cdot J(J+1)$.

Rotational constant $B = h/(8\pi I)$, where $I$ represents the moment of inertia $I = \mu R^2$ and $\mu$ is reduced mass. For diatomic molecules $\mu = m_1 m_2/(m_1 + m_2)$, in which case $R$ is the distance between two bonded atoms. The rotational constant of $\ce{^{127}I^{37}Cl}$ is $3.28\cdot10^{9}\ \mathrm{Hz}$.

a) Calculate bond length (in pm) in $\ce{^{127}I^{37}Cl}$ molecule.

Volatile molecular liquid $\ce{ClF3}$ is one of the most reactive chemical compounds known. It spontaneously ignites asbestos, wood, and other building materials. This substance was used in incendiary bomb attacks in World War II. $\ce{ClF3}$ reacts explosively with water and with most organic substances. Big amounts of this substance are used in nuclear fuel processing to produce $\ce{UF6}$ (g): $\ce{U(s) + 3ClF3(g) <=> UF6(g) + 3ClF(g)}$.

b) Write the Lewis structure for $\ce{ClF3}$.

c) Sketch drawing that shows $\ce{ClF3}$ molecular structure. Approximately predict bond angles and show them in your drawing.

In a closed evacuated container with excess solid uranium, some amount of $\ce{ClF3}$ was injected. The initial concentration of this gaseous substance in the container was 0.0453 M. When equilibrium in the container at 87 °C was established, the total pressure in the container was 1.69 atm.

d) Calculate the partial pressure of each gaseous substance in equilibrium.

Another interhalogen $\ce{ClF}$ reacts with $\ce{AsF5}$: $\ce{AsF5 + 2ClF -> [Cl2F]+[AsF6]-}$.

e) Suggest the best Lewis structure for cation $\ce{[Cl2F]+}$.

f) Choose the role of $\ce{AsF5}$ in this reaction:

• i) Lewis base or
• ii) Lewis acid.

Four interhalogen compounds between iodine and fluorine are known.

g) Which of these molecules is/are nonpolar:

• i) $\ce{IF}$,
• ii) $\ce{IF3}$,
• iii) $\ce{IF5}$,
• iv) $\ce{IF7}$.

problems.title: Organic juggling
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Organic juggling

Molecular rearrangements are very important in organic chemistry not only as a versatile synthetic method but also being mechanistically very interesting. In the course of such reactions, functional groups usually undergo changes and atoms' connectivity order is altered. One of the most famous reactions of this kind is a Favorskii rearrangement, discovered more than a hundred years ago. A typical example of this reaction is shown below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2006-5-fig1.png

Favorskii rearrangement could also work with other nucleophiles such as alkoxide or cyanide ions. Two alternative mechanisms, A and B, have been proposed for this reaction:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2006-5-fig2.png

In order to establish the real mechanism, a substrate with a radioactive carbon $\ce{^{14}C}$ label was synthesized according to the scheme:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2006-5-fig3.png

a) Draw the structural formulas of compounds $\mathbf{1}$–$\mathbf{10}$ and denote $\ce{^{14}C}$ atom with "*".

b) After the reduction of $\mathbf{5}$, two isomeric compounds, $\mathbf{6}$ and $\mathbf{7}$, were obtained. Only one of them, compound $\mathbf{7}$, reacts further to give a compound $\mathbf{8}$. Show stereochemical formulas of $\mathbf{6}$ and $\mathbf{7}$ and write the reaction mechanism with $\ce{NaH}$.

The reaction of $\mathbf{10}$ with $\ce{NaOMe}$ affords Favorskii rearrangement product $\mathbf{11}$.

c) Show the place of the radioactive label and its relative intensity (radioactivity) in compound $\mathbf{11}$ according to mechanisms $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$.

The product $\mathbf{11}$ was further degraded as shown below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2006-5-fig4.png

d) It was shown that the total radioactivity of all degradation's gaseous products is 25% less than that of a starting ester. Which mechanism explains this fact?

There are a number of reactions that proceed via the Favorskii-type mechanism.

e) Draw the structure of compounds $\mathbf{12}$–$\mathbf{14}$ and the reasonable mechanisms of its formation. The compound $\mathbf{13}$ has a strong vibrational band at $1670\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2006-5-fig5.png

f) What are the possible by-products when α-haloketones react under Favorskii reaction conditions?

problems.title: Killer lake
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Killer lake

Nyos is a low-activity volcanic lake. It is grievously known as a killer lake after a disaster happened in 1896 when the release of $\ce{CO2}$ gas from the lake's depths caused the death of 1746 people. According to one of the hypotheses, cold tropical rain cooled the "surface layer" (50 meters), which fell 130 meters down, displaced "deep water" and disturbed the equilibrium. As a result, the lake "has exploded" like a bottle of champagne.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \ce{CO2 (g)} & \ce{H2CO3 (aq)} & \ce{H2O (l)} \\ \hline \Delta H_\mathrm{f}^\circ & -393.5 & -699.0 & -285.8 \\ \hline \Delta S_\mathrm{f}^\circ & 213.8 & 190.0 & 70.1 \end{array}$$

Assume that the lake looks like a cylinder with a bottom surface area of $1.20\ \mathrm{km^2}$ and a height (depth) of 120 meters. The bottom of the lake is composed of $\ce{FeCO3}$, which is in equilibrium with $\ce{CO2}$ via dissolution. It is also known that the "surface-layer" water (50 meters) does not mix with the deeper layers; temperature at 50–180 meters depth approximately equals 23 °C. $K_\mathrm{a1}(\ce{H2CO3}) = 3.57\cdot10^{-7}$, $K_\mathrm{a2}(\ce{H2CO3}) = 4.40\cdot10^{-11}$, $K_\mathrm{sp}(\ce{FeCO3}) = 5.91\cdot10^{-11}$.

a) Calculate the constants $K_\mathrm{H} = [\ce{H2CO3 (aq)}]/p(\ce{CO2 (g)})$ value at 23 °C.

b) Calculate the pH at i) 50 and ii) 180 meters depth.

c) Determine the maximum solubility of $\ce{CO2}$ at i) 50 and ii) 180 meters depth.

d) Assuming the linear dependence of concentration on depth (50-180 meters), evaluate the maximum quantity, mass, and volume at 30 °C of $\ce{CO2}$ that could be emitted from the lake.

problems.title: Polar winter in Antarctic
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Polar winter in Antarctic

Nitric acid hydrates have received much attention as possible catalysts for heterogeneous reactions that bring about the Antarctic ozone hole. Worsnop et al. has measured thermodynamic parameters for sublimation of nitric acid mono-, di- and trihydrates at 220 K:

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l} & \Delta_\mathrm{r}G^\circ,\ \mathrm{kJ\cdot mol^{-1}} & \Delta_\mathrm{r}H^\circ,\ \mathrm{kJ\cdot mol^{-1}} \\ \hline \ce{HNO3*H2O(s) -> HNO3(g) + H2O(g)} & 46.2 & 127 \\ \hline \ce{HNO3*2H2O(s) -> HNO3(g) + 2H2O(g)} & 69.4 & 188 \\ \hline \ce{HNO3*3H2O(s) -> HNO3(g) + 3H2O(g)} & 93.2 & 237 \end{array}$$

a) Calculate $\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^\circ$ at 190 K (the conditions of the polar winter stratosphere). Assume that $\Delta_\mathrm{r}H^\circ$ and $\Delta_\mathrm{r}S^\circ$ do not depend on temperature.

a) Which hydrate is thermodynamically most stable at 190 K if $p(\ce{H2O}) = 1.3\cdot10^{-7}$ bar and $p(\ce{HNO3}) = 4.1\cdot10^{-10}$ bar? Standard pressure is 1 bar.

problems.title: Synthesis of bicyclic compound
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Synthesis of bicyclic compound

The bicyclic skeleton of compound $\mathbf{X}$ appears in many naturally occurring alkaloids. The simple approach to the synthesis of title compound is outlined in this problem. At the heart of the synthesis is a nitro-aldol reaction between benzaldehyde and nitromethane.

a) Explain, why nitromethane is acidic enough for an aldol reaction to occur?

b) Under basic reaction conditions benzaldehyde and nitromethane in nitro-aldol reaction give compound $\mathbf{A}$ (molecular formula $\ce{C8H7NO2}$). Based on the knowledge of the classical aldol reaction suggest structure of $\mathbf{A}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-2-fig1.png

c) $\mathbf{A}$ is fully reduced with hydrogen using palladium on charcoal as a catalyst to give $\mathbf{B}$ (molecular formula $\ce{C8H11N}$). $\mathbf{B}$ is fairly basic and readily forms salts with acids. Draw the structure of compound $\mathbf{B}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-2-fig2.png

d) $\mathbf{B}$ under acidic reaction conditions reacts with formaldehyde to give final compound $\mathbf{X}$. This transformation proceeds through formation of $\mathbf{C}$ (molecular formula $\ce{C9H11N}$), which under these reaction conditions undergoes cyclization to form bicyclic $\mathbf{X}$ (molecular formula $\ce{C9H11N}$). $\mathbf{X}$ is fairly basic and is usually isolated in a form of salt. Using your knowledge of reactivity of carbonyl compounds suggest structures of $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{X}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-2-fig3.png

problems.title: Isoleucine dating
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Isoleucine dating

The rate of isomerization of isoleucine in fossilized bone can be used as an indication of the average temperature of the sample storage.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-3-fig1.png

At 20°C this reaction has a half-life of 125000 years and its activation energy is 139.7 kJ/mol. After a very long time, the ratio allo/iso reaches an equilibrium value of 1.38. You may assume that this equilibrium constant does not depend on temperature.

The time dependence of concentration for a reversible reaction is given by equation:

$$\ln\left(\frac{[\mathrm{A}]-[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{eq}}{[\mathrm{A}]_0-[\mathrm{A}]_\mathrm{eq}}\right) = -\left(k_1+k_{-1}\right)t$$

For a hippopotamus mandible which lived near a warm spring in South Africa, the present allo/iso ratio in bones is 0.42. Radiocarbon dating, which is temperature independent, determined the age of hippo tooth, which was 38600 years.

a) Assuming that no allo was present initially, determine constants for forward and reverse reactions and overall isomerization constant ($k_1 + k_{-1}$).

b) Calculate an average conservation temperature of the hippopotamus remains in soil.

problems.title: Goblin’s element
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Goblin’s element

Metal $\mathbf{X}$ was discovered in 1735. Its name has derived from a German word meaning “goblin” or “evil spirit”.

A sample of metal $\mathbf{X}$ immersed in $\ce{H2O}$ weights 13.031 g. Meanwhile the weight of the same sample in $\ce{CCl4}$ is 12.046 g. The density of $\ce{CCl4}$ is $1.5940\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$.

In order to identify the metal $\mathbf{X}$, neutron diffraction is used. The diffraction pattern is specific to the FCC structure and the angle of the reflection ($2\theta$) from the (222) plane is 76.956°. The velocity of neutrons in the diffractometer is 3115.0 m/s.

The same sample is heated in $\ce{O2}$ atmosphere until metal X has reacted completely. The product of the reaction is compound $\mathbf{A}$ containing 26.577% of oxygen (by mass). All the amount of compound $\mathbf{A}$ reacts with diluted HCl releasing 1.0298 L of $\ce{O2}$ at 25.00ºC temperature and 100.0 kPa pressure, giving salt $\mathbf{B}$ and water only.

Compound $\mathbf{B}$ is dissolved in an aqueous solution containing $\ce{Cl^-}$, $\ce{Br^-}$ and $\ce{I^-}$ ions. Complex ion $\mathbf{C}$ forms as one of the products. The formula of ion $\mathbf{C}$ is $[\ce{XCl2Br2I2}]^{n-}$ and it is a paramagnetic.

Complex carbonyl compound $\mathbf{D}$ is prepared by heating metal $\mathbf{X}$ under a high pressure of carbon monoxide. The formula of compound $\mathbf{D}$ is $[\mathbf{X}_2\ce{(CO)8}]$ and it is a diamagnetic. The both atoms of metal $\mathbf{X}$ are equivalent in the structure of compound $\mathbf{D}$. A CO molecule donates a pair of electrons to form a single bond only but not all the CO molecules are equivalent in the structure of compound $\mathbf{D}$.

a) Calculate the density of metal $\mathbf{X}$ in $\mathrm{g/cm^3}$.

b) Calculate the unit cell parameter ($a$) of metal $\mathbf{X}$ in pm.

c) Calculate the molar mass of metal $\mathbf{X}$ in g/mol. What element is metal $\mathbf{X}$?

d) Write a chemical formula of compound $\mathbf{A}$.

e) Write a balanced chemical equation of the reaction of compound $\mathbf{A}$ with diluted HCl.

f) Sketch the spatial structures of all possible isomers (including structural, geometrical and optical) of ion $\mathbf{C}$.

g) Count the number of unpaired electrons in ion $\mathbf{C}$. Consider halogenides as weak field ligands

h) Sketch the spatial structure of compound $\mathbf{D}$.

problems.title: Sigmatropic rearrangement
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Sigmatropic rearrangement

Pericyclic reactions are concerted processes that occur by way of a cyclic transition state in which more than one bond is formed or broken within the cycle. The so called sigmatropic rearrangements constitute a large group of pericyclic reactions. Of all the sigmatropic rearrangements, the [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement has been used most in organic synthesis. The reaction involves the transformation of 1,5-dienes and all-carbon system is known as the Cope rearrangement, whereas with an allyl vinyl ether the reaction is termed a Claisen rearrangement. The examples of these reactions are given bellow:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-5-fig1.png

The sigmatropic rearrangement has been use in many syntheses of the complex molecules and has industrial applications as well.

1. The key step in the synthesis of the alkaloid strychnine was made by use of this chemistry:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-5-fig2.png

2. The chemical company BASF manufactures citral (intermediate in the synthesis of vitamin A) by the remarkable synthesis shown bellow:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2007-5-fig3.png

Write the reaction mechanism (except for the loss of water in the example 2) and possible intermediates for both reactions.

HINT: by treating acetaldehyde with ethanol under the same reaction conditions as in example 2, vinylethyl ether could be obtained.

problems.title: Dolomite
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Dolomite

One of the most widespread minerals is dolomite, which in huge amounts is also in bowels of the earth of Baltic States. Dolomite contains two metallic elements $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$. Metal $\mathbf{A}$ crystallizes in hexagonal close packed atomic structure (unit cell parameters: $a = 3.2094$ Å, $b = 3.2094$ Å, $c = 5.2108$ Å and $\gamma = 120^\mathrm{o}$), while metal $\mathbf{B}$ crystallizes in cubic close packed atomic structure (unit cell parameter: $a = 5.5884$ Å).

a) What are metals $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$? Calculate atomic radii for these elements!

b) Calculate by how many percent (of initial atomic radii) reduce radii for both metallic elements, when ions are produced from atoms. It is known that oxides of both elements have sodium chloride structure and radii of oxide anion is 1.28 Å. Unit cell parameters for both oxides are 4.213 Å un 4.811 Å, respectively.

Industrially metal $\mathbf{A}$ can be produced from sea water. To purify chloride of metal $\mathbf{A}$ from other salts hydroxide of metal $\mathbf{B}$ is added to sea water. The obtained white precipitate is dissolved in hydrochloric acid and evaporated, till metal $\mathbf{A}$ salt hydrate forms. Then the hydrate is heated and salt melted and electrolyzed.

c) Write down equations of all chemical reactions described above and calculate time for electrolysis which has to be performed to isolate 1.0 ton of metal $\mathbf{A}$. Current intensity 9.0 kA.

One of the most favorite reactions for students is burning of metal $\mathbf{A}$ in the air. Reaction produces huge amount of UV light and two binary compounds, one of them is oxide of metal $\mathbf{A}$.

d) What is the second compound that is produced in this reaction? Write equations of both reactions and propose chemical reactions which could be useful for experimental identification of this compound.

Metal $\mathbf{A}$ also is used in army of USA, for preparing food in field conditions. To heat food wrapped in aluminum foil a special heater (in English Flameless Ration Heater), which contains 30 mL water, is used. Heating material is a composite, where powder of metal $\mathbf{A}$ and iron are associated in matrix of high density polyethylene. In presence of chloride ions metal $\mathbf{A}$ reacts with water, forming hydroxide and hydrogen, which is available for burning to obtain extra heat.

e) Using thermodynamical constants shown below calculate minimal mass of element $\mathbf{A}$, which is needed for heating 1.0 L of water from temperature 20°C to 100°C. Assume that all chemical reactions proceed under standard conditions.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c} \text{Compound} & \Delta H_\mathrm{f,298}\ (\mathrm{kJ/mol}) & C_\mathrm{p}\ (\mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}) \\ \hline \ce{H2},\ g & 0 & 28{,}83 \\ \hline \ce{H2O},\ g & -241{,}81 & 33{,}61 \\ \hline \ce{H2O},\ l & -285{,}83 & 75{,}30 \\ \hline \text{Metal } \mathbf{A},\ s & 0 & 24{,}89 \\ \hline \text{Hydroxide of metal } \mathbf{A},\ s & -924{,}66 & 76{,}99 \end{array}$$

f) Metal $\mathbf{A}$ hydroxide, which forms in reaction, is slightly soluble. Calculate solubility (mg/L; milligrams per liter) of mentioned hydroxide in distilled water. $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{s} = 11{,}25$.

problems.title: A mysterious substance
problems.problem:
Problem 1. A mysterious substance

Part I.

Compound $\mathbf{A}$ is an oxide and compound $\mathbf{D}$ is a salt (sulfate). Using chemical equations and data given below, identify compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$. Support your answers with calculations.

$$\begin{array}{ll} (1) & \mathbf{A} + \ce{3NaOCl + 4NaOH} \rightarrow 2\mathbf{B} + \ce{3NaCl + 2H2O}\quad (\mathrm{pH} > 7) \\ (2) & 4\mathbf{B} + \ce{6H2O} \rightarrow 2\mathbf{A}\cdot\ce{H2O} + \ce{8NaOH + 3O2}\quad (\mathrm{pH} = 7) \\ (3) & \mathbf{D} + \ce{3Na2O2} \rightarrow \mathbf{C} + \ce{Na2SO4 + O2} \\ (4) & 3\mathbf{C} + \ce{5H2O} \rightarrow \mathbf{A} + \mathbf{B} + \ce{10NaOH} \end{array}$$

The color of the solution, containing compound $\mathbf{B}$, is deep red-purple. If 0.10 g of compound $\mathbf{C}$ is dissolved in 100 $\mathrm{cm^3}$ distilled water, the pH of the solution becomes 12.2 ($\mathbf{B}$ fully dissociates).

a) Write chemical formulas for compounds $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$.

Part II.

Wustite is a mineral form of iron(II) oxide. It is a non-stoichiometric compound as it is always Fe-deficient and is formulated as $\ce{Fe}_{1-x}\ce{O}$ ($0.04 < x < 0.11$). To counter the charge imbalance caused by $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ vacancies, some $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ ions are present in the lattice.

b) How many $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ ions are needed to counter one $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ ion vacancy?

c) Express the ratio $n(\ce{Fe^{3+}})/n(\ce{Fe^{2+}})$ as a function of $x$.

Iron atoms in wustite form a face-centered-cubic lattice. The oxygen atoms occupy octahedral gaps between iron atoms.

d) Calculate the lattice constant and the distance between the two closest iron atoms (in Å) in wustite ($\ce{Fe_{0.925}O}$, density $6.02\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$).

e) Calculate the distance between the two closest oxygen atoms in wustite.

f) Express density as a function of $x$, assuming that the lattice parameter does not change in the given interval of $x$.

problems.title: Cobalt-Chameleon
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Cobalt-Chameleon

Cobalt is one of the most well-known metals. Since ancient times, cobalt salts have been used to color glass and make enamels. Various cobalt compounds were found in sculptures of ancient Egypt, Persian jewelry, and among the remains of the city of Pompey.

For more than 100 years, scientists have been interested in complex cobalt salts, in which the oxidation state of the metal is +3 rather than the more common +2.

a) Using the given Latimer diagram of cobalt, prove mathematically whether it is possible for cobalt(II) to undergo disproportionation in acidic media. Explain why the more stable oxidation state for complex cobalt ions is +3, whereas for classical cobalt ions it is +2.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2008-2-fig1.png

At the end of the 19th century, investigations of cobalt complexes with amines gained high popularity, for example, compounds with a general formula $[\ce{Co(NH3)}_{6-x}\ce{Cl}_{x}]\ce{Cl}_{3-x}$, where $x$ is a small natural number.

b) Write all possible isomers for compounds with this general formula, assuming that the coordination number of cobalt is 6 and the oxidation state is +3.

c) The stability of complex ions can be evaluated based on electrochemical measurements. Using the given data, calculate the stability constants for cobalt(II) and cobalt(III) complexes with amines.

At the beginning of the 20th century, complexes of cobalt with organic molecules were widely investigated, for example, the well-known cobalt complex with ethylenediamine (en).

d) Write the formula of this compound, provide the structures of all possible isomers and explain the difference in physical properties of these isomers. What type of ligands does ethylene diamine belong to? In this regard, what is its difference from ammonia and chloride anion?

It is well-known that $d$-orbitals can be split into numerous sublevels by the ligand field.

e) Provide a diagram of split $d$-orbitals of the cobalt in $\ce{[Co(NH3)6]Cl3}$ complex. For every energy level, give the index of the $d$-orbital from which the new orbital was formed. Explain your choice.

f) Based on the spectrum provided below, calculate the energy difference between $d$-orbitals.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2008-2-fig2.png

problems.title: Negative activation energy!?
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Negative activation energy!?

According to the results of the investigation, the direct reaction $\ce{2NO(g) + O2(g) <=> 2NO2(g)}$ has a negative apparent activation energy.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} & [\ce{NO}],\ [\mathrm{M}] & [\ce{O2}],\ [\mathrm{M}] & r = \mathrm{d}[\ce{NO}]/\mathrm{d}t,\ [\mathrm{M\,s^{-1}}] \\ \hline 1 & 0.010 & 0.010 & 2.5\cdot10^{-5} \\ \hline 2 & 0.020 & 0.010 & 1.0\cdot10^{-4} \\ \hline 3 & 0.010 & 0.020 & 5.0\cdot10^{-5} \end{array}$$

a) Determine the partial reaction orders based on the data given in the table.

b) Calculate the rate constant $k$.

The rate constant ($k'$) of the reverse reaction at $327\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $372\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is 83.9 and 407 $\mathrm{M^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$.

c) Calculate the activation energy of the reverse reaction ($E_\mathrm{a}'$).

d) Calculate the reaction enthalpy $\Delta H_\mathrm{r}$ according to the data given in the table.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} & \ce{NO} & \ce{NO2} \\ \hline \Delta H_\mathrm{f}\ [\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}] & 90.29 & 33.10 \end{array}$$

e) Sketch the reaction energy diagram in the coordinates energy vs reaction coordinate, and mark $E_\mathrm{a}$, $E_\mathrm{a}'$, $\Delta H_\mathrm{r}$ on it.

Based on experimental data, the following reaction mechanism was suggested:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2008-3-fig1.png

f) Derive the rate equation.

g) Decide whether the suggested mechanism supports kinetic and thermodynamic data. Explain why the value of the apparent activation energy is less than zero and the dependence of the rate constant of a direct reaction on temperature

problems.title: An elegant compound of the last century
problems.problem:
Problem 4. An elegant compound of the last century

The target compound $\mathbf{G}$ in this problem is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon. It was first synthesized in 1964 by Professor Erich Clar at the University of Glasgow. At the time of the synthesis, this type of compound was associated with the investigation of theoretical problems of aromaticity. In modern times, with the rapid developments in the field of nanoscience, these compounds find their use as novel materials used as liquid crystals and synthetic “metals”.

Draw the structural formulas of compounds $\mathbf{A}$−$\mathbf{G}$ in the scheme provided below. Pay particular attention to the following notes:

(1) Dicarboxylic acid $\mathbf{A}$ is the major isomer of all the possible products in this acylation reaction.

(2) In compound $\mathbf{B}$, there is only one new ring formed.

(3) Compound $\mathbf{D}$ is pentacyclic.

(4) The $\ce{^1H}$ NMR spectrum of compound $\mathbf{E}$ has three sets of signals with relative intensities of 1 : 1 : 3.

(5) The last chemical transformation is lousy in terms of chemical yield but it does provide an elegant structure $\mathbf{G}$.

problems.title: Li-ion battery
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Li-ion battery

Video cameras, smartphones, laptops, etc, require a portable power source – batteries. The ideal battery is reliable, lightweight, long-lasting, stable, and environmentally safe. A battery consists of anode, cathode, and electrolyte.

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l|l|l} \text{Metal} & \ce{Li} & \ce{Ca} & \ce{Al} & \ce{Cd} \\ \hline \rho\ [\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}] & 0.53 & 1.54 & 2.70 & 8.64 \\ \hline E^\circ\ [\mathrm{V}] & -3.04 & -2.87 & -1.66 & -0.40 \end{array}$$

The table provides density and standard potential for metals that are usually used as anodes.

a) Write the half-reactions of these metals.

b) Calculate the electrochemical capacity of these metals. The electrochemical capacity is defined as the maximal quantity of electric charge produced per 1 g of metal ($\mathrm{A\,h\,g^{-1}}$).

c) Which metal is most suitable for the battery anode? Provide two reasons.

The standard reduction potential of water is −0.83 V.

d) Write the reduction reaction of water.

e) Which of the listed metals react with water at room temperature? Write the reaction equations and explain the answer.

f) Calculate the equilibrium constant for the reaction between water and lithium. Is the process spontaneous? Provide an explanation.

The ions solvate in the electrolyte during the oxidation of the metal. The formed solution must be a good electrolyte. Lithium hexafluorophosphate(V) is added to the solvent to increase its electrical conductivity.

g) Which of the solvents: (a) water, (b) ethanol, (c) dimethyl sulfoxide, (d) hexane is the most suitable for a lithium battery? Provide an explanation.

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l|l|l|l|l} \text{Compounds} & \ce{Bi2O3} & \ce{FeS2} & \ce{LiCl} & \ce{Li2O} & \ce{Li2S} & \ce{CuCl2} \\ \hline \Delta G_\mathrm{f}^\circ & -493 & -160 & -384 & -562 & -439 & -382 \end{array}$$

h) Draw the spatial structures of dimethyl sulfoxide and lithium hexafluorophosphate(V) using the VSEPR model. Write the hybridization and partial charge of S and P atoms.

Sulfides, oxides and halogenides are used as materials for cathodes.

i) Write the equation of the total reaction in the lithium battery if the cathode is (a) $\ce{Bi2O3}$, (b) $\ce{FeS2}$, (c) $\ce{CuCl2}$ and the metal will be released as an element. For which battery (a-c) is the maximum non-expansion work of the reaction largest?

$\ce{FeS2}$ was used as the cathode of the lithium battery and the electrolyte was $\ce{LiPF6}$ solvated in dimethyl sulfoxide.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2008-5-fig1.png

j) Write the shorthand notation of the lithium battery. Write the cathodic half-reaction and calculate its standard potential.

k) Rewrite on the block diagram of the lithium battery: Li, $\ce{FeS2}$, lithium hexafluorophosphate(V), „+“, dimethyl sulfoxide, anode (A), cathode (K), electrolyte and engine. Mark the direction of the movement of electrons in the outer circuit.

l) Which material should be in excess in the lithium battery? Why?

problems.title: Supramolecular basket
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Supramolecular basket

It is well known that carboxylic acid methyl esters react with tertiary amines:

$$\ce{R-COO-CH3 + R3N ->} \ldots\ (\mathbf{1})$$

Compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are esters, which react with quinuclidine $\mathbf{C}$ in the same manner as is shown in reaction $\mathbf{1}$. Despite the fact that atoms near ester groups in compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are exactly the same, the quinuclidine reaction with ester $\mathbf{A}$ in mesitylene (1,3,5-trimethylbenzene) completes in 3 minutes, however, the reaction of compound $\mathbf{B}$ and quinuclidine at the same conditions is so slow that it is practically not observed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2008-6-fig1.png

The three-dimensional structures of compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are as follows:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2008-6-fig2.png

problems.title: Hydrolysis of pyrophosphate
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Hydrolysis of pyrophosphate (10 pts)

Let’s take a look at the hydrolysis of pyrophosphate ($\ce{P2O7^{4-}}$) by the enzyme. It is assumed that the concentration of pyrophosphate is much lower than the Michaelis constant; thus, the reaction is formally supposed to be first-order. At pH = 7 at 25 °C the apparent first-order rate constant is $k_7^* = 0{,}0010\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The mechanism of the hydrolysis is as follows:

$$\ce{H2P2O7^{2-} <=> HP2O7^{3-} <=> P2O7^{4-} -> 2HPO4^{2-}}$$

where $\mathrm{p}K_1 = 6.12$ ja $\mathrm{p}K_2 = 8.95$ are the acid dissociation constants (1st and 2nd stages), and $k$ is the true rate constant which does not depend on pH (3rd stage). It is assumed that acid dissociations are fast compared with the hydrolysis.

a) Write down the equations for the acid dissociation constants $K_1$ and $K_2$, and derive an expression of pyrophosphate total concentration.

b) Calculate the value of true rate constant $k$.

c) Calculate the values of apparent rate constants $k_6^*$ and $k_8^*$ at pH = 6 and pH = 8.

problems.title: Iodine and polyiodides
problems.problem:
Problem 2. Iodine and polyiodides (12 pts)

Iodine was discovered in 1811 by the French chemist Curtois during the process of manufacturing potassium nitrate, with which he supplied the Napoleon armies. While washing seaweed ashes with sulphuric acid, he noticed violet fumes that condensed on his copper equipment and caused corrosion. Below you see diagram that represents some iodine chemistry. Only iodine containing substances $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{H}$ are indicated in this diagram. In some cases it might be more reaction products.

a) Identify substances $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{H}$ and write appropriate balanced molecular chemical equations:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2009-2-fig1.png

One of remarkable features of iodine is possibility to form so called polyiodide ions. One of the simplest polyiodide ion present in tincture of iodine. This tincture is prepared by dissolution of iodine $\ce{I2}$ in a solution of $\ce{KI}$. In this mixture triiodide ions $\ce{I3^-}$ present. Until now anions from $\ce{I2^-}$ to $\ce{I29^{3-}}$ have been established.

b) Write Lewis structure for $\ce{I3^-}$ ion. Don’t forget to indicate lone pairs of electrons. Show geometrical arrangement of iodine atoms in this ion.

c) Draw possible geometrical structures of $\ce{I5^-}$ ion. In this case you might omit lone pairs of electrons.

Polyiodides are not very stable compounds, but large cations with a high symmetry can be used to obtain thermally stable polyiodides. In the laboratory polyiodide $\mathrm{R_4NI}_{2x+1}$ ($x$ = 1, 2, 3, 4 ...) with large cation was investigated. R is radical of alkane. For titration of 0.219 g of $\mathrm{R_4NI}_{2x+1}$ 10.23 mL of 0.112 mol/L $\ce{Na2S2O3}$ solution was consumed. In the course of titration $\ce{S2O3^{2-}}$ is converted into $\ce{S4O6^{2-}}$.

d) Determine molecular formula of $\mathrm{R_4NI}_{2x+1}$. Clearly show your calculations.

problems.title: Small rings fighting diabetes
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Small rings fighting diabetes (10 pts)

The scheme shown below represents the industrial synthesis of a new class of drugs for treatment of type 2 diabetes. The synthesis, remarkable in its simplicity and especially in effortless purification of products, is used to produce the target molecule in kilogram quantities for clinical development.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2009-3-fig1.png

problems.title: Uses and misuses of nitrogen compounds
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Uses and misuses of nitrogen compounds (10 pts)

The thermal decomposition of urea at 175 °C affords the highly symmetrical, acidic ($\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a1} = 7$) compound $\mathbf{A}$ (composition: C 27,9%, H 2,3%, N 32,6%, O 37,2%) along with colorless gas $\mathbf{B}$. Compound $\mathbf{A}$ exists in solution as a mixture of isomers $\mathbf{A1}$ and $\mathbf{A2}$, where aromatic isomer $\mathbf{A1}$ is the predominant form.

$\mathbf{A}$ can be converted into two different chlorides $\mathbf{C1}$ (N 22,8%) and $\mathbf{C2}$ (N 18,1%). $\mathbf{C1}$ is well suited for multiple functionalizations with nucleophiles and is commonly used as a precursor in production of pesticides and fluorescent dyes, while $\mathbf{C2}$ found its widespread use as water disinfectant and bleaching agent.

Although it is not commercially viable, compound $\mathbf{D}$, in principle, could be obtained from $\mathbf{C1}$ and gas $\mathbf{B}$. $\mathbf{D}$ has very high nitrogen content (66,6%). The use of $\mathbf{D}$ in dairy products to artificially boost protein content was at the core of the scandal in China in 2008.

$\mathbf{C1}$ is also widely utilized in organic synthesis. The wide range of reagents based on $\mathbf{C1}$ allows simple one step transformation of a carboxylic acid into amide, ester and even into alcohol. Sequentially treating $\mathbf{C1}$ with methanol then N-methylpiperidine (NMP) affords coupling agent $\mathbf{E}$ (N 20,4%) in a form of the chloride salt.

Coupling reagent $\mathbf{E}$ is primarily used in the synthesis of various amides. Although $\mathbf{E}$ is cheap and easy to use, which allows the synthesis even on multikilogram scale, it has one significant drawback. The reaction solvent choice is limited to tetrahydrofuran. In other solvents, like chloroform or acetonitrile, $\mathbf{E}$ undergoes rapid degradation with formation of neutral compound $\mathbf{F}$ (N 25,0%) and gas $\mathbf{G}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2009-4-fig1.png

1. Provide structures of compounds $\mathbf{A1}$, $\mathbf{A2}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C1}$, $\mathbf{C2}$, $\mathbf{D}$, $\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{G}$. (1 pt each, $\mathbf{B}$ is 0,5 pt)

2. Suggest simple solution to avoid degradation of activating agent $\mathbf{E}$. (0,75 pt)

3. Draw the mechanism of conversion of carboxylic acid $\ce{RCOOH}$ into amide $\ce{RCONHR'}$, using activating agent $\mathbf{E}$. (0,75 pt)

problems.title: Ethanol as sourse of energy
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Ethanol as sourse of energy (10 points)

Since ancient times ethanol has been used for lamp oil and cooking, along with plant and animal oils. Nowadays vast majority of ethanol is used as fuel and is produced in large scale by fermentation, in which certain species of yeast metabolize sugar producing ethanol. It can be said that sunlight is used to run the engine of a vehicles, as a simple sugar is created in the plant by photosynthesis, and during ethanol combustion carbon dioxide and water are produced with a release of energy.

a) Write chemical equations for sugar synthesis, ethanol production and combustion.

Early in 1860 Nikolaus August Otto used ethyl alcohol as a fuel in internal combustion engine. Today ethanol may be used as a fuel to power both direct-ethanol fuel cells (DEFC) and combustion engines. One of the first DEFC, which schematic diagram is given, was introduced in the ShellEco-Marathon in 2007.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2010-1-fig1.png

b) Identify chemical species $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{F}$ on figure.

c) From thermodynamic data calculate DEFC maximal energy conversion efficiency ratio: $\eta = \Delta_\mathrm{r}G^0/\Delta_\mathrm{r}H^0$ (25 °C).$^1$

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{compound} & \ce{O2} & \ce{H2} & \ce{CO2} & \ce{H2O} & \ce{C2H5OH} & \ce{C6H12O6} \\ \hline \Delta H^0,\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} & 0 & 0 & -394 & -286 & -278 & -1273 \\ \hline S^0,\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} & 205 & 131 & 214 & 70 & 161 & 212 \end{array}$$

$^1$ Give all the ansvers with two signifant numbers.

d) For comparison calculate efficiency of combustion engine running on Otto cycle using equation for maximal efficiency: $\eta = 1 - 1/r^{(\gamma-1)}$, where $\gamma = C_\mathrm{p}/C_\mathrm{V} \approx 1.4$, $r$ is compression ratio which equals 9 and 12.5 for ethanol and gasoline, respectively. Assume, that only half of the efficiency is achieved in practice.

There are several unsolved issues concerning DEFC, thus, in closer perspective it is more promising to convert ethanol into hydrogen in order to use the latter in typical hydrogen fuel cell.

e) Using given data calculate the maximal energy conversion efficiency ratio ($\eta = \Delta_\mathrm{r}G^0/\Delta_\mathrm{r}H^0$) of the hydrogen fuel cell.

To be realistic, it should be considered that in order to move a vehicle the electric energy must be converted into mechanical. Let's assume that conversion efficiency of subsystems are: 90% for invertor, 90% for motor, and 90% for gas compressor. Overall conversion efficiency ratio may be compared to energy conversion efficiency ratio of combustion engine in which chemical energy is directly converted to mechanical.

f) Estimate overall efficiency of hydrogen vehicle.

g) Name one-two main advantages of i) ethanol over gasoline fuel in internal combustion engine; ii) fuel cell over internal combustion engine.

a) In the water solution the chromium(III) perchlorate is presented as aquachromium cation with co-ordination number equal to six. Write the formula of aquachromium cation and the precipitate $\mathbf{X}$.

b) During the reflux the water in the inner sphere of the complex is replaced by anion. Write the equation of reaction.

c) The solubility product of the salt $\mathbf{X}$ is $K_\mathrm{sp} = 2.9\cdot10^{-3}$ at 0 °C, but it is possible to dissolve 10.9 g of the salt in $5\underline{0}$ g water at 100 °C ($\rho = 1.1\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$). Calculate how many grams of salt $\mathbf{X}$ did precipitate during the cooling process.

$^2$ The problem is based on T.W. Swaddle, E.L. King Inorg. Chem. 4 (1965) 532.

d) The reaction mixture contained various complexes of chromium. Cation-exchange (contains $\ce{R-SO3H}$ groups) separation allowed isolation of hexaaquachromium(III) ions, fluoropentaaquachromium(III) ions, difluorotetraaquachromium(III) ions and hydrolytic dimers of chromium. During the eluation process the sample was first taken into the column and afterwards the ions were eluated out using $\ce{HClO4}$ with varing concentration. The contents of chromium and fluoride in purified fluoropentaaquachromium(III) ions was established. $10.0\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ of the sample was first decomposed using the alkaline solution of hydrogen peroxide. The fluoride ion is liberated and the oxydation state of chromium changes from III to VI. After that the sample was divided into two equal parts. First part was acidified using conc. $\ce{HCl}$ and then 3 g $\ce{KI}$ was added. After standing 5 min the solution was titrated using $18.5\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ 0.0975 M $\ce{Na2S2O3}$. The endpoint was determined using starch solution. The second part was analysed using the fluoride ion selective electrode which was calibrated using solutions with known concentration of $\ce{F-}$. The equation of calibration curve was $E = 183\,\mathrm{mV} - 56\,\mathrm{mV}\cdot\log\left[\ce{F-}\right]$. The reading of the voltmeter was 252.6 mV and the final volume of the solution was $1\underline{0}\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ after adjusting the pH of the solution to six.

e) Write all the equations of chemial reactions in the analysis process and calculate the ration of $n(\mathrm{F})/n(\mathrm{Cr})$ in the sample.

The pseudo first order rate coefficient of aquation of fluoropentaaquachromium(III) ion

$$\ce{[Cr(H2O)5F]^{2+} + H+ + H2O = [Cr(H2O)6]^{3+} + HF}\quad(\mathbf{I})$$

is

$$k = \frac{2.303\left(\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_0 - \left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_\infty\right)}{t\left(\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_0 + \left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_\infty\right)}\log\frac{\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_0^2 - \left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]\,\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_\infty}{\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_0\left(\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right] - \left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_\infty\right)}$$

where $\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_0 = 5.28\cdot10^{-3}\,\mathrm{M}$ is the starting concentration and $\left[\ce{CrF^{2+}}\right]_\infty$ equilibrium concentration of the complex ion.

f) Calculate the time $t$ (h) needed to aquate $7\underline{0}\%$ of the complex ion at 77.2 °C if the concentration of hydrogen ions is 0.414 M, the rate constant is $4.40\cdot10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and equilibrium constant of the reaction is 0.048. The water is in excess and not included in the equilibrium constant.

The hydrofluoric acid is weak acid.

g) Calculate $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}(\ce{HF})$ at 25ºC if the equilibrium constant of the

$$\ce{[Cr(H2O)6]^{3+} + F- = [Cr(H2O)5F]^{2+} + H2O}\quad(\mathbf{II})$$

problems.title: Asymmetry without asymmetric center
problems.problem:
Problem 3. Asymmetry without asymmetric center (10 points)

Allenes are not only versatile starting materials in organic synthesis but also present an interesting case of molecular chirality. Since it is quite difficult to synthesize allenes in stereoselective manner, they are first obtained as racemic mixture and then resolved into individual enantiomers. One of the ways of synthesizing allenes in depicted below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2010-3-fig1.png

a) Identify symmetric structure $\mathbf{A}$. Keep in mind that this reaction is not very efficient and $\mathbf{A}$ is only one of few possible products in this reaction.

b) Provide the mechanism for conversion of $\mathbf{A}$ into an allene.

One of the methods to produce allenes in pure enantiomeric form is dynamic resolution of racemic mixtures. The method takes advantage of quick epimerization and the low solubility of one of the stereoisomers. Epimerization means interconversion of one enantiomer into another proceeding through a common intermediate $\mathbf{B}$ (see scheme below). Since all of the compounds are in the equilibrium, the position of the equilibrium is shifted in the direction of the less soluble stereoisomer, which is then collected as a precipitate.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2010-3-fig2.png

Reaction conditions: room temperature, $\ce{Et3N}$ (0.05 Eq), pentane; R* is (-)-menthyl

c) Provide the structure of $\mathbf{B}$.

In order to establish the absolute configuration of the allene $\mathbf{X}$ obtained by dynamic resolution, one can follow a method developed by Agosta in 1964. To better understand the essence of the method let us consider all transformations performed on BOTH enantiomers.

The allene ester is first hydrolyzed to dicarboxylic acid and then in Diels-Alder reaction with cyclopentadiene is transformed into a mixure of separable products.

$$\mathrm{R^{*}O_2CHC{=}C{=}CHCO_2R^{*}} \xrightarrow{\text{a)}} \underset{\text{Single enantiomer}}{\mathrm{HO_2CHC{=}C{=}CHCO_2H}} \xrightarrow{\text{b)}} \mathbf{C}_{1\text{-}4}$$

a) $\ce{NaOH}$; b) cyclopentadiene

d) Provide structures for ALL possible adducts with cyclopentadiene that could be formed from EACH allene enatiomer ($\mathbf{C}_{1\text{-}4}$ from one allene enantiomer, and $\mathbf{C}_{5\text{-}8}$ from the other). You are allowed to use molecular models provided by organizers.

[In the answer space, the left structure below heads the column for $\mathbf{C}_{1\text{-}4}$ and the right structure the column for $\mathbf{C}_{5\text{-}8}$:]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2010-3-fig3.png

Each of the individual compounds $\mathrm{C}_{1\text{-}8}$ is then subjected to 2 test reactions: a) iodolactonization and b) cyclic anhydride formation.

$$\mathbf{D} \xleftarrow{\text{a)}} \mathbf{C} \xrightarrow{\text{b)}} \mathbf{E}$$

a) $\ce{I2}$, $\ce{NaHCO3}$; b) acetic anhydride

e) In your list of adducts, identify which structures $\mathbf{C}_{1\text{-}8}$ are capable of giving desired products in BOTH test reactions. Draw equation for ONE iodolactonization reaction ($\mathbf{D}$) and ONE cyclic anhydride formation ($\mathbf{E}$).

The compound(s) $\mathbf{C}$ that gives positive result in both test reactions is (are) then degraded according to the following scheme. The product of the reaction $\mathbf{F}$ ($\ce{C7H10O}$) is optically active compound.

$$\mathbf{C} \xrightarrow{\text{a)-d)}} \mathbf{F}\quad \ce{C7H10O}$$

a) Pd/C, $\ce{H2}$; b) $\ce{CH2N2}$; c) $\ce{O3}$; d) $\ce{HCl}$, reflux

In summary, the explicit assignment of the absolute configuration by method of Agosta is based on the fact that one enantiomer of $\mathbf{F}$ can only be produced from (R)-allene, while the opposite enantiomer of $\mathbf{F}$ stems only from the (S)-allene.

f) In aforementioned case of dynamic resolution of allenes the degradation yields exclusively (1S,4R)-$\mathbf{F}$ stereoisomer. Draw the structure of $\mathbf{F}$.

g) Based on the structure of compound (1S,4R)-F and identification method by Agosta suggest the structure of allene $\mathbf{X}$, which was obtained by dynamic resolution.

problems.title: Environmental hazards
problems.problem:
Problem 4. Environmental hazards (10 points)

Around World War II Jinzu River in Toyama prefecture Japan was contaminated with element $\mathbf{X_1}$ compounds and nowadays Japan still is one of top three producers of this element. Element $\mathbf{X_1}$ accumulates in rice and can cause Itai-Itai disease in humans; it also replaces calcium in bones. This element is produced from compound $\mathbf{A}$ which is its only mineral of practical importance. Compound $\mathbf{A}$ is also a direct band gap semiconductor and has many applications for example in light detectors and as thermally stable pigments.

Binary compound $\mathbf{A}$ contains also nonmetallic element $\mathbf{Y_1}$ and this compound forms minerals greenockite (first discovered in Scotland and named after the land owner Lord Greenock) and hawleyite. The first mineral has hexagonal structure while second mineral has cubic structure. Mass fraction of $\mathbf{X_1}$ in compound $\mathbf{A}$ is 77.6%.

Element $\mathbf{X_1}$ can be obtained from $\mathbf{A}$ by roasting it in air. Obtained oxide is treated with sulfur trioxide to form $\mathbf{X_1}$ sulfate which is dissolved in water and electrolyzed.

a) Determine element $\mathbf{X_1}$, show your calculations!

b) Write equations for all mentioned reactions taking place in element production!

c) Calculate mass of metal $\mathbf{X_1}$ which can be obtained by electrolysis of 0.15 M metal sulfate solution with 0.5 A current and one hour long.

d) Write electron formula for element $\mathbf{X_1}$ ions in sulfate solution, knowing that there are no f electrons in this ion.

e) Table with lattice parameters for greenockite and hawleyite is shown bellow. Calculate $Z$ value (number of “molecules” in unit cell) for hawleyite as well as density for greenockite.

Cell parameters of minerals are given below:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Parameter} & \text{Greenockite} & \text{Hawleyite} \\ \hline \text{System} & \text{hexagonal} & \text{cubic} \\ \text{Parameters} & \begin{array}{c} a = b = 3.82\ \text{Å} \\ c = 6.26\ \text{Å} \\ \gamma = 120^\mathrm{o}\ \text{(angle between } a \\ \text{and } b\text{)} \end{array} & a = 5.818\ \text{Å} \\ Z & 2 & ? \\ \text{Density} & ? & 4.87\ \mathrm{g\cdot cm^{-3}} \end{array}$$

Practically important is also compound $\mathbf{B}$ which is used for production of solar energy panels and which contains nonmetallic element $\mathbf{Y_2}$. Mass fraction of element $\mathbf{X_1}$ in compound $\mathbf{B}$ is less than 50% and it is known that element $\mathbf{Y_2}$ is in same group as element $\mathbf{Y_1}$ but electronegativity for element $\mathbf{Y_2}$ is smaller than for $\mathbf{Y_1}$.

f) Determine element $\mathbf{Y_2}$, show your calculations!

Usually element $\mathbf{X_1}$ is found together with element $\mathbf{X_2}$ which is placed in same group in periodic table. Binary compound of element $\mathbf{X_2}$ with $\mathbf{Y_1}$ crystallizes in cubic face centered crystals (FCC) with parameter $a = 5.406$ Å. Density of this compound is $4.09\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$.

g) Determine element $\mathbf{X_2}$, show your calculations!

h) Order all possible binary compounds from elements $\mathbf{X_1}$, $\mathbf{X_2}$, $\mathbf{Y_1}$ and $\mathbf{Y_2}$ in order of increasing covalent bond content and decreasing ionic bond content!

Elements $\mathbf{X_1}$ and $\mathbf{X_2}$ can be separated also due to different solubilities of their hydroxides. Hydroxides and carbonates are the forms of $\mathbf{X_1}$ compounds which are now found in Jinzu River bed ($\mathbf{X_1}$ concentration aprox. 2 ppm).

i) Which element ($\mathbf{X_1}$ or $\mathbf{X_2}$) hydroxide has better solubility in alkaline solutions? Explain it with atomic structure of elements.

It is possible to answer next question without answering previous ones!

j) Calculate solubility (express in mol/L) of both compounds in water pH = 10.0! Take into account complex ion formation! All necessary data are given in table In the table logarithms of the overall formation constants are given.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c} & \mathbf{I} & \mathbf{II} \\ \hline \mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{sp}\ \text{of hydroxide} & 14.14 & 16.5 \\ \mathrm{p}K_1 & 4.17 & 4.40 \\ \mathrm{p}K_{1,2} & 8.33 & 11.30 \\ \mathrm{p}K_{1,2,3} & 9.02 & 14.14 \\ \mathrm{p}K_{1,2,3,4} & 8.62 & 17.66 \end{array}$$

problems.title: Half solid half melted
problems.problem:
Problem 5. Half solid half melted (10 points)

In 1914, Tubandt and Lorenz showed that solid silver iodide above 147 °C transforms into $\alpha$-AgI modification that is good electrical conductor. Temperature of 147 °C may be considered as melting point for silver ion sublattice. The remaining iodide ion sublattice is stable until 557 °C. It was determined that iodide ions form body centered cubic (BCC) sublattice with lattice constant (lattice parameter) $5.04\cdot10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m}$.

In picture the principal scheme of Tuband’s electrochemical cell is shown.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/bcho-2010-5-fig1.png

In this cell silver electrodes 0.1000 g each were placed in contact with both sides of solid $\ce{AgI}$ pellet Then electric current of 35.2 mA was flowed for 15.5 min. After that silver electrodes where taken off the pellet and were placed into two labelled $100.0\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ volumetric flasks (label “Solution A” for anode and “Solution B” for cathode). Excess of diluted $\ce{HNO3(aq)}$ was added into both flasks. After dissolution of metallic electrodes both volumetric flasks were filled with distilled water till calibration mark. Solution A and Solution B were used for titration of $10.00\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ samples of $0.0113\,\mathrm{mol\cdot dm^{-3}}$ $\ce{NaCl}$ solution that contains small amount of $\ce{K2CrO4}$. Endpoint for these titrations were appearance of brick-red precipitate.

a) Write half-reactions that represent what was happening at the anode and at the cathode during the electric current flow.

b) Write balanced chemical equation that is proceeding during action of diluted nitric acid $\ce{HNO3(aq)}$ onto electrodes.

c) Write formula of the brick-red compound that precipitates at the titration endpoint.

d) Calculate the ratio V(Solution A)/V(Solution B) (ratio of volumes of respectively solutions that were used up for the titration of samples of $\ce{NaCl}$ solution).

e) Determine radius of iodide ion in BCC sublattice.

f) Calculate density of solid $\ce{AgI}$ conductor.

g) $\ce{AgI}$ is light sensitive compound suitable for photography. After development of black-white photo the image should be “fixed” by dissolving away all remaining silver iodide (or other silver salts). Sodium thiosulfate $\ce{Na2S2O3}$ is suitable fixing agent. Under reaction with silver iodide it produces compound that contains 26.9% of silver by mass. Write chemical equation that shows what is happening during the “fixing” black-white photo.

problems.title: Modafinil – work without sleep ?
problems.problem:
Problem 6. Modafinil – work without sleep ? (10 points)

Modafinil was originally created to treat narcolepsy (a condition when a person falls asleep at inappropriate times), but it spread widely among students and businessmen. Although a productive day after a sleepless night sounds unbelievable, it is not the only effect of modafinil; it also acts as an antidepressant and improves memory in some cases. Modafinil has a considerably smaller list of side effects than caffeine but due to its unknown long-term effects it remains a prescription drug. Yet this doesn’t scare most of its users off, who buy it from the internet shops or illegal dealers.

An industrial synthesis scheme of Modafinil is presented below. In the $^1$H NMR spectrum of compound $\mathbf{A}$ there is one singlet (6.0 ppm) and ten times more intensive multiplet (7.3 ppm). After treating compound $\mathbf{A}$ with sodium hydrosulfide a side product $\mathbf{C}'$ was detected, therefore to avoid its formation one additional step was introduced in the synthesis.

a) Draw the structural formulas of all letter-named compounds.

Modafinil is actually a mixture of two enantiomers, where only the R isomer shows the indicated biological activity.

problems.title: Aluminium
problems.problem:
Problem 1. Aluminium (6 points)

Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the Earth‘s crust. Some compounds of aluminium, like alum (the double sulphate $\ce{KAl(SO4)2*12H2O}$) were in use since ancient Greece time.

a) The freezing point depression constant for water is $K_\mathrm{f} = 1.86\,^\circ\mathrm{C\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$. Calculate the freezing point of the solution prepared by dissolving $9.48\,\mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{KAl(SO4)2*12H2O}$ in $100.0\,\mathrm{g}$ of water.

b) The most important ore of aluminium is bauxite, which consists from $\ce{Al2O3}$ and impurities. Bauxite can be purified by dissolving in concentrated $\ce{NaOH}$ solution. Write molecular equation that shows what is happening when $\ce{Al2O3}$ reacts with $\ce{NaOH}$ solution.

c) After removal of insoluble impurities, weak acid is added to the solution obtained in part b and $\ce{Al(OH)3}$ is precipitating. Solubility product $K_\mathrm{SP}$ for $\ce{Al(OH)3}$ is $1.3\cdot10^{-33}$ (at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$). Calculate mass of pure $\ce{Al(OH)3}$ that can be dissolved in $10.0\,\mathrm{L}$ of pure water at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid or its salts) is among the most important and widely used reagents in titrimetry. Unfortunately, this reagent is not good for direct determination of aluminium ions, because EDTA reacts with aluminium ions too slowly. Problem can be solved by applying back titration method. In the beginning EDTA and aluminium compound solution are allowed to react in the hot solution for several minutes, and then excess EDTA can be fast and easily titrated with $\ce{Zn^{2+}(aq)}$. Analysis is performed in presence of buffer solution. Reactions taking place in this method can be represented as:

$$\ce{Al^{3+} + EDTA^{4-} -> Al*EDTA^-}$$

and

$$\ce{Zn^{2+} + EDTA^{4-} -> Zn*EDTA^{2-}}$$

d) $20.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ of solution, that contains $\ce{Al^{3+}}$, was transferred into flask that contains $50.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ $0.0500\,\mathrm{M}$ EDTA solution. problems.title: Smart robot

Problem 4. Smart robot (13 points)

The hero of the movie “Star Wars” – a very intelligent robot R2-D2 received $20.0\,\mathrm{mg}$ of radioactive sample $\mathbf{P}$ known to contain only element $\mathbf{A}$.
